title: Trump brings two divided Cabinet heavyweights to China as controversy hangs over high-stakes talks
summary: President Donald Trump said Scott Bessent and Howard Lutnick hold opposing views on China as both join his high-stakes Asia trip to meet Xi Jinping.
story: NVIDIA chip investigations escalate as President Donald Trump prepares to meet with three world leaders, including Chinese President Xi Jinping. Heritage Foundation chief economist E.J. Antoni joins co-hosts Charlie Hurt, Ainsley Earhardt and Lawrence Jones on 'Fox & Friends' to analyze the national security stakes.

President Donald Trump is bringing two powerful Cabinet officials divided over restrictions on China's access to advanced American AI chips on his high-stakes Asia trip, as controversy over the issue follows them into talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick are both accompanying Trump on the four-day trip despite reports of a dispute over whether to blacklist a company suspected of helping China obtain restricted American AI technology. Trump acknowledged their competing views Monday and suggested Lutnick may have delayed action to avoid worsening relations with Beijing.

"He might have delayed it, but he was doing that because you could have if you didn't delay it. If you didn't do something, you could have a blow up with China. We're having a very good relationship with China right now, and I understand both sides of it, and I'll make a decision. But I understand very well both sides," the president said.

The dispute follows reports that Lutnick resisted efforts to place Singapore-based Megaspeed on a U.S. trade blacklist, despite Trump reportedly supporting action against the company on three occasions this year, according to Axios. Megaspeed has faced allegations that its operations helped Chinese companies gain access to restricted Nvidia chips.
TWO TOP TRUMP CABINET OFFICIALS GO TO WAR OVER CHINA SPY SCANDAL AMID EXPLOSIVE ACCUSATIONS: REPORT

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent speaks with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick prior to an event with President Donald Trump and Apple CEO Tim Cook in the Oval Office of the White House on Aug. 6, 2025, in Washington, D.C. Apple announced a $100 billion investment in U.S. manufacturing facilities, on top of a February commitment to a $500 billion investment in the U.S. economy and 20,000 new jobs over the next four years. (Win McNamee/Getty Images)

The Commerce Department announced a new rule this week aimed at preventing Chinese companies and other restricted foreign entities from accessing advanced American computing technology through data centers in third countries. The department said the rule was written at the direction of the Treasury Department and National Security Council.
Trump told reporters Monday he is not considering replacing Lutnick, saying "he's done a very good job."

Bessent publicly confirmed Friday that several administration departments had supported adding Megaspeed to the Commerce Department's Entity List, which would restrict the company's access to U.S. technology.
"Treasury, War, USTR and State — they were in favor of putting Megaspeed on the Entity List for months, but Commerce has the pen," Bessent said.
The Commerce Department denied Axios' account of a confrontation between Bessent and Lutnick in the White House Situation Room, saying the two officials had no such conversation.
Trump is bringing several of his administration's most powerful officials on the four-day Asia trip, which includes stops in the Philippines and China.
TRUMP TO CONFRONT XI AT HIGH-STAKES SUMMIT OVER CHINA BACKING FOR IRAN, RUSSIA

President Donald Trump, alongside Secretary of Treasury Scott Bessent, left, and Secretary of Commerce nominee Howard Lutnick, speaks to the press as he signs an executive order to create a U.S. sovereign wealth fund, in the Oval Office of the White House on February 3, 2025, in Washington, D.C. (Jim Watson/AFP via Getty Images)

The delegation includes Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Bessent, Lutnick, White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer and National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett, among other officials, a White House official confirmed to Fox News Digital.

Trump is expected to meet with world leaders, participate in regional economic and security summits and hold high-stakes talks with Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin, and possibly North Korea leader Kim Jong Un.

The controversy has also drawn attention to Nvidia's leadership. Nvidia announced Thursday that CEO Jensen Huang had resigned following reports about his relationship with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive suspected by U.S. intelligence of spying for China.
Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing and said Sunday that it retained outside counsel to investigate allegations surrounding its operations.
Trump said Monday it has not been confirmed she is a spy.
FEDERAL PROSECUTOR WARNS SEN WARREN OF 'LEGAL CONSEQUENCES' IF RECORDS AREN'T PRESERVED IN TRUMP-LINKED PROBES

China's first lady Peng Liyuan, China's President Xi Jinping, President Donald Trump and U.S. first lady Melania Trump pose on the North Portico steps of the White House ahead of a State Dinner in Washington, D.C., on September 24, 2026. (SAUL LOEB/AFP via Getty Images)

Lutnick, the former chairman and CEO of investment firm Cantor Fitzgerald, is one of the wealthiest officials to serve in a presidential administration. A longtime Trump ally, he co-chaired the president's 2024 transition team, and the two have known each other for decades through New York's business and social circles.
Lutnick has also agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 10 amid growing scrutiny of the Commerce Department's handling of Nvidia chip exports to China, CBS News reported.

Sens. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., and Chris Coons, D-Del., jointly called on the administration to preserve records related to Nvidia's advanced AI chip exports and potential national security risks. title: Trump leaves door open to Kim Jong Un joining high-stakes talks with Xi, Putin
summary: Trump suggested Kim Jong Un could appear during his China trip, saying the North Korean leader's presence is up to Xi Jinping ahead of trilateral talks in China.
story: President Donald Trump is set to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin during his Asia trip, and he left open the possibility that North Korean leader Kim Jong Un could join the high-stakes talks.
President Donald Trump offered a brief, unexpected response about North Korea during a White House gaggle Monday, adding a new wrinkle to his closely watched trip to Asia this week.
Trump suggested North Korean leader Kim Jong Un could make an appearance during his China trip, telling reporters, "We might have Kim Jong Un. He may come, I don’t know. That’s up to President Xi."

The comment came in response to a reporter's question about the upcoming high-stakes meetings between Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin at the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, China, and whether the trio planned to discuss North Korean nuclear capabilities.
PRESIDENT TRUMP TO HOLD HISTORIC TRILATERAL SUMMIT WITH XI AND PUTIN
President Donald Trump is expected to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin Thursday. (Reuters)

Trump and Kim last met in 2019, when their Hanoi summit ended without an agreement on North Korea’s nuclear program. Nonetheless, Pyongyang has since expanded its nuclear and missile capabilities, while efforts to restart talks have stalled. In August, Trump said he expected to meet Kim "later this year," but North Korea pushed back, with Kim Yo Jong saying the leaders’ relationship remained "excellent" while accusing Washington of maintaining hostile policies toward Pyongyang, Fox News Digital reported at the time.

Meanwhile, a U.S. official said last week, according to ABC News, that there were no plans for North Korea engagement during Trump’s Asia trip, and experts say the country is unlikely to feature prominently in the trilateral talks.

South Korean news outlet Yonhap News Agency reported Monday that South Korea’s Foreign Ministry said it hoped high-level talks on the sidelines of the APEC summit would contribute to peace and stability on the Korean Peninsula. South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun reportedly raised the possibility of renewed U.S.-North Korea dialogue at the summit with his Chinese counterpart, Wang Yi, in Beijing on Friday, stressing that South Korea has vital interests in Korean Peninsula issues and hopes that its perspective is taken into account.
NORTH KOREA MISSILE COULD PUT GUAM IN RANGE AS KIM REBUFFS TRUMP OUTREACH: EXPERT
President Donald Trump meets with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un at the North Korean side of the border at the village of Panmunjom in Demilitarized Zone, on June 30, 2019. (Susan Walsh/AP)

The South Korean news agency also reported Monday that Andrew Yeo, a senior fellow at the U.S.-based Brookings Institution, said North Korea’s nuclear program is unlikely to be discussed at the summit, citing differences between Washington and Moscow over Pyongyang’s nuclear ambitions. The report also highlighted comments from Korea Economic Institute senior fellow Ellen Kim, who reportedly suggested the leaders could briefly discuss North Korea behind closed doors, but nuclear arms control and the war in Iran are likely to take priority. Ellen Kim added that Xi or Putin could relay a message from Trump to Kim Jong Un, though they may be reluctant to support U.S.-North Korea negotiations for fear of losing influence over Pyongyang.
The trilateral meeting is scheduled for 2:30 p.m. Thursday local time at Shenzhen Kylin Villa, according to Trump’s public schedule.

White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales said Friday that Trump planned to discuss nuclear arms reduction with Xi and Putin, while a senior U.S. official said Iran would also be on the agenda. The Associated Press reported Monday that Trump plans to raise Russia’s war in Ukraine at the meeting as well.

title: Fetterman's Gaza-born challenger calls to 'abolish ICE,' oust top Democratic leaders
summary: Gaza-born socialist Ahmed Moor challenged one of Israel's strongest Senate supporters while calling for an overhaul of Democratic leadership.
story: Progressive Ahmed Moor is running to beat Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., in 2028, and is running in the opposite direction of the lawmaker’s current positions, including bucking the war in Iran and abolishing ICE.
FIRST ON FOX: It’s a circumstance almost ripped from a screenplay: a Gaza-born political newcomer wants to topple one of the Senate’s staunchest supporters of Israel in the Democratic Party.
But for Ahmed Moor, a member of the Democratic Socialists of America who is the first to toss his hat into the arena to challenge Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., the story doesn't end there.

"Look, so this race is not about John Fetterman," Moor told Fox News Digital in an interview. "John Fetterman's story is over, but the story of the United States continues. I'm getting in now because I believe we're in the midst of a constitutional crisis."
GAZA-BORN DEMOCRATIC SOCIALIST LAUNCHES PRIMARY BID AGAINST SEN JOHN FETTERMAN
Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., makes his way to votes in the U.S. Capitol on Sept. 30, 2026. (CQ-Roll Call, Inc. via Getty Images)

"I have some compassion for John Fetterman — I want to depersonalize," he continued. "Let's talk about policy. The policies that man has expressed and committed to are just a reflection of the special interests which have run his office for too long now. The problem of John Fetterman's policies is the problem of corruption in America."

Fetterman is up for re-election in the 2028 cycle and has become a target for Democrats in Pennsylvania ready to replace him as he continuously moved more to the center of the political spectrum and aligned with Republicans on key issues like the war in Iran, government funding and immigration.

Whether he runs again for a second term remains in the air. When asked by Fox News Digital if he had made a decision, Fetterman said, "The more, the merrier," to challengers entering the Democratic primary.
But Moor, so far, is the only candidate officially in the race.
FETTERMAN WARNS THERE IS NO LONGER 'COMMON GROUND' WITH FAR-LEFT DEMOCRATS OVER ISRAEL
"I know, he seems to really love Hamas," Fetterman said. "And now, so, like, so if you tell him, say thank you for running."
Moor was born in Gaza before immigrating to Philadelphia, where he went to public schools, attended the University of Pennsylvania and later went to Harvard to obtain a public policy degree.

His policy positions are in line with the growing progressive flank in the Senate Democratic caucus and echo the positions that Fetterman first ran on in 2022 when he pledged to support the Senate’s progressive standard-bearer, Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., if he won.

"I spent a lot of time on international policy, kind of a foreign policy specialist, one of the reasons the Senate job appeals to me," Moor said. "But equally, I'm committed to what I call the ‘Dignity Agenda,’ which is universal access to healthcare, childcare and affordable housing."

Among the top concerns for Moor in the "constitutional crisis" he sees in the country is freedom of speech, which he contended came under assault during the Biden administration when protests against "the genocide in Palestine" exploded across college campuses.
FETTERMAN PLAYS POLITICAL MAVERICK, BUT HIS VOTING RECORD TELLS ANOTHER STORY

Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., during a news conference following Senate Democrat policy luncheons at the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C., March 3, 2026. (Graeme Sloan/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

"Students were brutalized for assembly, for speech," Moor said. "That shouldn't happen in America. Donald Trump stepped through that breach and accelerated the assault. And ICE today is the worst expression, the violation of due process in America."
Like other Democrats and progressives, Moor wants to abolish Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), but he would "like to see immigration law enforced."

"ICE is a lawless organization — ICE is a paramilitary militia. ICE is not law enforcement," he said. "Let's abolish ICE. Let's hold the bad actors who've killed Americans and kidnapped others in our streets. Let's hold them to account for breaking our local ordinance and our local laws. That's a criminal matter today in America. I hope local prosecutors run with it."
Ahmed Moor, 42, a member of the Democratic Socialists of America, announced that he will run for a U.S. Senate seat occupied by Sen. John Fetterman. (Ahmed Moor/Getty Images)

And like other progressives who scored stunning victories during the midterm elections to help flip the Senate, like Sens.-elect Abdul El-Sayed and Peggy Flanagan, Moor is against the old guard of Democratic leadership staying in charge.

It’s a position that is gaining steam in the Senate, where Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., is mounting a rare challenge to Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., to lead Democrats through the forthcoming majority in the upper chamber.
Moor said Schumer and House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., both have to go.

"Chuck Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries don't have what it takes to meet the moment. They need to be replaced," Moor said. "This campaign is also about sustaining pressure in that direction. If they survive the leadership contest, which is underway today, I'm going to continue to sustain the pressure on both of those men to do the right thing continuously."

title: Seattle mayor orders park named for American president renamed
summary: Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson ordered Jackson Park renamed, citing Andrew Jackson's legacy of forcibly displacing Native American peoples from their lands.
story: XX-XY Athletics owner Jennifer Sey and high school athlete Frances Staudt join 'America Reports' to discuss Washington State's initiative to protect girls' sports as Democrats push to block the effort.
Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson has ordered a city park named after President Andrew Jackson to be renamed to better fit "the values of our city."

The city argues that Jackson's legacy includes policies that forcibly displaced Native American peoples from their ancestral lands. Wilson directed the Seattle Parks and Recreation to begin a community renaming process on Monday. The 160-acre Jackson Park plays host to the Jackson Park Golf Course.

"We’ve heard from community members who want to change the name of Jackson Park, and now is the right time to move this conversation forward. With new light rail connections and opportunities to make the park more accessible and welcoming, we should have a park that reflects the values of our city," Wilson said in a statement.
WASHINGTON AG'S OFFICE INDICATES IT WILL DEFEND GIRLS' SPORTS BALLOT MEASURE AFTER ACLU SUES TO BLOCK IT
Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson at a shooting vigil on Monday. (Getty Images)
"I’m directing Seattle Parks and Recreation to begin a community naming process to find a name that better reflects this place, its history, and the people who enjoy it," she added.
The renaming effort comes just days after Wilson also backed an effort to block a girls sports initiative that overwhelmingly passed a statewide vote.
SEATTLE MAYOR BACKS EFFORT TO BLOCK GIRLS' SPORTS INITIATIVE THAT PASSED IN 36 OF WASHINGTON'S 39 COUNTIES

Wilson said last week that she supports the Seattle School Board's unanimous vote to pursue legal action against Initiative 638 — which would enforce separation of boys and girls in K-12 sports in Washington state.

title: Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson faces audit calls after CFO quits over 'financial integrity' concerns
summary: Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson faces fresh budget turmoil after CFO Ashlee Gabrysch abruptly resigns, questioning the city's financial reporting and budget calculations.
story: Chicago Fraternal Order of Police president John Catanzara discusses crime in Chicago after a violent repeat offender was accused of murdering a 7-year-old girl and Mayor Brandon Johnson’s response on ‘America Reports.’

Chicago’s chief financial officer, who formerly worked for a top credit ratings bureau, resigned Friday citing financial integrity concerns, casting a shadow over the fiscal management of progressive Mayor Brandon Johnson amid a fight over the FY-2027 budget.

Chicago CFO Ashlee Gabrysch served only three months before the onetime Fitch Ratings executive stepped down, saying she could no longer meet her professional obligations under the conditions of her employment, according to a resignation letter obtained by the Chicago Tribune.

"The chief financial officer’s statements about the city’s finances are relied upon by investors, rating agencies, City Council, and taxpayers, and they must be complete and accurate," Gabrysch wrote, according to the Tribune.
"I am not able to fulfill those obligations under the conditions in which I have been asked to serve."

Johnson did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment, but his press secretary accused Gabrysch of being "largely absent" during key parts of the next budget’s creation process.
CHICAGO MAYOR CALLS ICE RAIDS ‘TERRORISM,’ SAYS TRUMP'S AMERICA APPEARS AS ‘IF THE CONFEDERACY WON’

The mayor's office also accused Gabrysch of improperly directing a $75 million payment to city pension funds before the required legal procedures had been completed, saying it would refer the matter to Chicago's Office of Inspector General for review.
The Tribune recounted recent events in the budget process involving Gabrysch, including that she disagreed with Johnson over assertions about the size of the city’s deficit.

In September, Johnson announced that the Windy City faces a projected $882 million budget shortfall in 2027, which local media described as smaller than a typical election year and lighter than the $1.15 billion deficit projected in 2025. The city holds its elections in odd years.

"We have difficult and consequential decisions ahead of us as we work to address the structural financial challenges that have confronted Chicago for decades," Johnson said at the time, according to Chicago’s PBS affiliate.
However, according to the Tribune, Johnson claimed the true figure is now $662 million, "adjusted" in concert with planned borrowing to help fund settlement amounts involving police officers.
CHICAGO MAYOR CALLS DOGE AN ‘ACT OF WAR’

Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson's press secretary accused Gabrysch of being "largely absent" during key parts of the next budget’s creation process. (Eileen T. Meslar/Chicago Tribune/Tribune News Service via Getty Images)

Gabrysch challenged that accounting during budget hearings, arguing that the settlement expenses should remain part of the deficit and that borrowing to pay them amounted to a temporary fix rather than a lasting solution.
While the administration maintained that 76% of its budget measures addressed underlying financial problems, Gabrysch calculated the figure at just 56%, according to the Tribune.

Alderman Marty Quinn, D-Midway, questioned Johnson’s handling at the time, according to the paper, saying he was "not surprised that the mayor may be a little disingenuous here, that seems to be his normal course."

Gabrysch also stopped short of calling Johnson's proposed $17.6 billion budget balanced during an October City Council hearing, arguing that the city needed to demonstrate progress toward reducing future deficits, according to Crain's Chicago Business.

City Comptroller Michael Belsky maintained that proposed revenues matched expenditures, while acting Budget Director Jonathan Ernst defended the administration's calculations and its plan to borrow roughly $480 million to cover legal settlements.
Gabrysch warned that the city anticipated issuing $350 million in settlement-related bonds in 2027, with an estimated $190 million in interest costs over seven years, according to Crain's.

Her resignation prompted Council Finance Committee chairman Pat Dowell, D-South Loop, to call for an independent audit.

The departure adds to a wave of turnover in Johnson's financial leadership, including two previous CFO departures this year and the resignation of the city's budget director in August. The upheaval comes as Chicago grapples with mounting financial obligations and credit-rating downgrades.

title: Radical activist with decades-old socialist ties emerges behind Dems' under-the-radar midterm operation
summary: Heather Booth, an 80-year-old socialist feminist, built the American Accountability Network's covert social media campaign that shaped midterms.
story: Silicon Valley tech pioneer Allison Huynh warns of a socialist surge within the Democratic Party as the Democratic Socialists of America endorses candidates on the ballot. Huynh, who is a former Obama fundraiser, discusses the far-left's radical agenda and its threat to the party's future.

A coordinated social media operation aimed at influencing voters ahead of the midterm elections was led in part by an 80-year-old socialist organizer who spent decades helping build the modern left's activist infrastructure, according to tax records reviewed by Fox News Digital.

"The Republicans never figured out what we were doing," political commentator Van Jones said earlier this month on CNN's "The Source" with Kaitlan Collins. "There’s something called the American Accountability Network: tens of thousands of online humans, not bots, coordinated to make the affordability message a winning message online … Don’t get mad at me. I was given permission to reveal this."

The American Accountability Network (AAN), which incorporation documents show was founded in early 2025, is an online activist organization that recruited both large content creators, as well as everyday Americans, and tasked them with posting, sharing and otherwise amplifying rhetoric that framed Democrats as the party of affordability — a message that exit polls suggest resonated with the electorate.

Tax documents identify the woman behind the effort as Heather Booth, AAN’s president and an 80-year-old self-described "socialist feminist" who has been deeply involved in far-left activism since the anti-war movement of the Vietnam era.
DEMOCRATS SAY THEY'LL MAKE LIFE AFFORDABLE. YOUR WALLET MAY DISAGREE
Van Jones speaks onstage during the 2025 ForbesBLK Summit at Ray Charles Performing Arts Center Morehouse College on October 10, 2025, in Atlanta, Georgia. (Paras Griffin/Getty Images)
Podcaster and former FBI Deputy Director Dan Bongino didn't buy into Jones' claims that AAN played a large part in determining the midterm elections earlier this month.

"Are influencers really influencing you? Or are the influencer days numbered as people wake up to the grift. Folks, I'm leaning more towards the latter," Bongino said on the Nov. 9 episode of his show. "I don't buy any of this. ... Maybe they had some effect in certain places. My humble opinion, I don't believe it ... I'm not sure the social media ecosystem had the effect Van Jones is saying it does. I heard the same thing, the exact same argument was used to say Donald Trump stole the election through Russian Facebook ads. And that was crap, too."
"Van is selling himself for the next campaign; I'm not buying it," Bongino told Fox News Digital.

Booth's decades of socialist activism are documented extensively in the historical record, including in her own correspondence. In the mid-1970s, Booth and her husband were key allies of the Democratic Socialist Organizing Committee, a precursor to the Democratic Socialists of America, helping the fledgling organization build ties with community groups and draft a high-profile manifesto aimed at pushing the Democratic Party economically leftward, according to letters Booth wrote in 1975.

Booth also disclosed in an interview that she was a founding member of the Chicago chapter of the Women’s International Terrorist Conspiracy from Hell (WITCH), what she described as a "guerrilla theater" group that staged provocative protests ranging from releasing mice at a bridal fair, staging mock curses against financial institutions and using hair and nail clippings in a mock hex protesting the dismissal of a women’s liberation activist who advocated overthrowing capitalism from the University of Chicago.

In a 1972 socialist feminist manifesto, Booth and her co-authors advocated for disarming police, publicly funded abortions and significant redistribution of wealth, while describing capitalism as an "institutionalized form of oppression."
Booth’s late husband, whom she worked closely with throughout her career, was no less prolific or radical than she was.
RADICAL SOCIALIST WING'S HUGE NIGHT REVEALS ASCENDING CLOUT WITHIN DEMOCRATIC PARTY
Heather Booth, who started the Jane Collective, stands for a portrait at her house in Washington, D.C., on May 27, 2022. (Photo by Stefani Reynolds/AFP)

Paul Booth is credited with authoring portions of the Port Huron statement, which framed American anti-communism as corrosive to democracy, proposed transferring certain national powers to international institutions as part of disarmament and called for greater democratic control of economic life.

Booth’s husband also served as national secretary of Students for a Democratic Society, a leading New Left organization that fractured in 1969 amid ideological infighting, with one faction giving rise to the militant Weather Underground. While Heather was also an SDS member who left before the Weathermen seized control, not all of her activism was legally above board.

In interviews, Booth has admitted to founding Jane, or the Abortion Counseling Service of Women’s Liberation, an organization that helped women obtain over 11,000 underground abortions before the Supreme Court mandated that the practice be legal nationwide in 1973. Law enforcement arrested seven women working for the organization in 1972 for abortion and conspiracy to commit abortion, though the charges were dropped following the court’s decision.

As Jane’s operations shuttered, Booth turned to a new aim: training the next generation of activists. Booth helped establish Midwest Academy, which incorporated in 1972 and began offering general organizing training in 1973, building an institution that says it has trained more than 50,000 organizers.
AAN, Jones and Booth did not respond to requests for comment when reached by Fox News Digital.

While the individuals who lead AAN through their midterm messaging campaign are clearly disclosed in tax forms, the funding behind the effort is more opaque. Nonprofit tax disclosures operate on a roughly one-year delay, meaning that financial information is only available for its 2025 tax year, when most of its election-related activities occurred in 2026.
MEMBER OF LARGEST TEACHERS UNION IN US CLAIMS ORG IS 'NO LONGER FOCUSED ON CHILDREN,' ONLY 'POLITICAL POWER'

Civil Rights activist Heather Booth speaks onstage during The 2022 MAKERS Conference at Waldorf Astoria Monarch Beach on October 25, 2022, in Dana Point, California. (Photo by Vivien Killilea/Getty Images for The MAKERS Conference)
What tax documents do exist, however, begin to paint a picture of the financial forces behind AAN’s social media push.

Of the roughly $280,000 AAN reported raising in 2025, $200,000 came from the American Federation of Teachers, the second-largest teachers labor union in America, according to its LM-2 disclosure. Receiving approximately 70% of its funding from a labor union during its inaugural year of operation was not AAN’s sole link to organized labor, however.

Midwest Academy, where Booth still serves as chairwoman, has done considerable work training union officials over the course of its history. Union financial disclosures show that labor unions such as the National Education Association, AFL-CIO, American Federation of Teachers (AFT) and the Service Employees International Union (SEIU) have collectively pumped roughly $2 million into the organization Booth founded since 2020.

Booth also directed the AFL-CIO’s healthcare campaign in 2008, helped run SEIU unionization efforts, and her late husband was a longtime American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees (AFSCME) organizer and leader, according to her website and oral histories about her life.
'DARK MONEY’ GROUP ACCUSED OF 'SCHEME' TO TIP ELECTION IN FAVOR OF DEMOCRATS, MANIPULATE GOP VOTERS
Voters cast midterm election ballots in the social hall at St. Patrick's Church in Youngstown, Ohio, on Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. (Jeff Swensen/Getty Images)
The '70s-era radical was not the only AAN leader to have ties to the labor movement.

Rio Tazewell, the director of the organization, has served on working groups alongside union leadership and Reggie Hubbard, identified as a leader on incorporation documents, works with major unions on education efforts and has a board seat at a union-backed nonprofit. AAN’s public-facing website, in fact, identifies the AFL-CIO, AFT, SEIU and AFSCME as organizations it has worked with.

AAN partnered with an organization called DemCastUSA, which has received $613,500 from the SEIU since 2022, to promote at least some of its social media amplification efforts. Former Democratic Sen. Doug Jones, who received significant support from organized labor during his political career, sits on DemCastUSA’s board.

As AAN worked to amplify Democratic messaging across social media ahead of Election Day, Americans viewed Republicans as more politically extreme than Democrats, according to Gallup polling. The survey found that 59% of Americans considered the Republican Party too extreme, compared with 43% who said the same of Democrats. AAN’s social media boosting strategy sought to reinforce favorable perceptions of Democrats and pin Americans’ economic anxiety on GOP policies, though the polling does not establish whether the campaign influenced those views.

Alongside DemCastUSA, AAN ran a program called "Amplifier Army" that aimed to give left-of-center voices a privileged slot in social media algorithms by coordinating interactions that would give such posts a larger reach.

"Together, we're building a network of organizers, creators and everyday people who use their social media to flood the feed with the content and calls to action that move this fight forward — at the inflection points where public pressure actually shifts the outcome," a sign-up page for the program reads. Participants are invited to "share coordinated priority content at the moments that matter most" and "amplify calls to action from movement partners across all major platforms."
FAR-LEFT GROUPS PIVOT FROM MAY DAY PROTESTS TO MOBILIZE VOTERS FOR 2026 MIDTERMS, PUSHING DEMS LEFTWARD
Concerns are growing about non-disclosed political advocacy across social media. (WLDavies/iStock/Getty Images)

Fox News Digital attended an Amplifier Army training session earlier in November, obtaining an audio recording, screenshots of the pitch deck shown to participants, a link to the program’s group chat and an invitation online platform used to coordinate social media engagement.

The WhatsApp group chat only has around 80 members. However, during the training session, the organizer in charge mentioned that they had recently created a new chat because their original forum on Signal had reached maximum capacity. The maximum number of participants in a Signal chat is 1,000.

At the end of the presentation, participants were instructed to create an account on an online app called ProSocial. The platform feeds an array of posts to users, all from mid-to-large Democratic-aligned social media accounts, and instructs users to like, comment, share, save and repost the content in question. Points are assigned for each action and the individual who gets the most points at the end of every month receives a prize from the organization.

A slide included in the training session’s slide show indicated that posts with partnered accounts selected for amplification saw a double-digit increase in shares and likes relative to posts from partners held back from amplification at random. Fox News Digital was not able to independently verify this data.

The organizer running the training session claimed that those behind the Amplifier Army coordinated with socialist activists in Brazil to help build their system, seeking to emulate the online push that helped Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva win an upset victory in Brazil’s recent presidential election.

Despite the considerable reach AAN claims for its social media operation, questions remain about how much influence the effort actually had on the midterm elections. Increased energy costs, rising grocery bills and stubbornly high housing prices, for instance, gave Americans reasons to be dissatisfied with the administration, regardless of what they did or didn’t see on social media.

Additionally, even with a thousand active members dutifully boosting posts curated by AAN, it is unclear how much of a difference that could have made on social media platforms trafficked by billions of users.

That said, AAN claims to include massive left-leaning media outlets in its network, including ​​MeidasTouch, which consistently generates hundreds of millions of monthly views and downloads.

title: Trump's immigration olive branch threatens to open Pandora's box as experts warn of far-reaching fallout
summary: Donald Trump's amnesty signal sparks fierce debate among immigration experts over rule of law, assimilation and the fiscal cost of legalization.
story: Steven Camarota of the Center for Immigration Studies (CIS) discouraged an amnesty deal as President Donald Trump considers working with Democrats on immigration.

After President Donald Trump signaled in a "60 Minutes" interview that aired shortly after the midterm elections that he was willing to "work on a deal" with Democrats to allow some illegal immigrants to gain legal status, Fox News Digital spoke with several immigration experts about the potential ramifications of such an agreement.

The interview came just days after Republicans suffered crushing losses in the midterm elections, raising questions about whether Trump might be willing to compromise on immigration. But the president later ruled out amnesty, saying, "There won't be amnesty," while maintaining that his immigration policy had not changed.

While Trump has not outlined a specific proposal, his comments have raised questions about what a potential deal could look like and how granting legal status to some illegal immigrants could impact the rule of law, assimilation and fiscal policy.
TRUMP ADMITS IMMIGRATION ENFORCEMENT MAY HAVE BEEN TOO 'TOUGH' IN FIRST INTERVIEW SINCE MIDTERMS

President Donald Trump signed two executive orders on Sept. 19, 2025, establishing the "Trump Gold Card" and introducing a $100,000 fee for H-1B visas. The "Trump Gold Card" is a visa program that allows foreign nationals permanent residency and a pathway to U.S. citizenship for a $1 million investment in the United States. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)
Fox News Digital spoke with three immigration experts about what a potential agreement could mean for the country, including its impact on the rule of law, assimilation and taxpayers.
Rule of Law:

"I think one of the first things we have to always consider is the impact on the rule of law and does it undermine it. It's very hard to argue that the best way to restore the rule of law and deal with illegal immigration is to reward some large fraction of people who've broken the law," said Steven Camarota, the director of research at the Center for Immigration Studies (CIS).
Camarota believes that amnesty begs the question of basic fairness, and impacts how people who have come to the United States legally view the immigration system.
"It seems like it mocks them," he said.

He used the example of a person who illegally overstays a visa to illustrate his point, saying that person shouldn't be rewarded with citizenship after overstaying a visa, especially when there are millions of people who have already followed the law and left the country when their visas expired.
Laura Collins, director of immigration policy at the George W. Bush Presidential Center, acknowledged those concerns but argued that the country's immigration laws are part of the problem.
AMERICA NEEDS WORKERS, BUT TRUMP'S POLICIES ARE SHARPLY CUTTING LEGAL IMMIGRATION

"I understand people's concerns about the rule of law," said Collins. "I also think you have a set of immigration laws that are not working as intended. The reason we have so many people who are here undocumented is because we have an economy that pulls in a lot of people's work, but an immigration system that restricts that labor flow."
Immigrants take the oath of citizenship to the United States during a naturalization ceremony at Liberty State Park on Sept. 19, 2014, in Jersey City, New Jersey. (John Moore/Getty Images)

She says the United States is at a crossroads: the country can choose a system where illegal immigrants cannot stay and fix their mistakes while also contributing to the economy, or they can stay and be offered a chance at restitution.

"Almost every single piece of legislation that has had a chance at passage on immigration that involves legalization program has had things like paying back taxes, going through a background check, paying some sort of fine or fee or restitution payment in order to make up for the fact that these people did something illegal by either overstaying a visa or crossing the border," she said.
But Camarota questioned whether a future amnesty agreement would actually require immigrants to complete those restitution payments before obtaining citizenship.
Assimilation:
Camarota also said that one of the main reasons for restricting immigration in the first place is to ensure that the United States isn't overwhelmed.

"We don't want the numbers to be so large that they overwhelm the assimilation process, where you can go to a school where everyone's from your background or you don't ever have to learn English, because there's enough people around you who you don't [and] who you speak your native tongue So that's one reason to limit immigration," he said.

President Donald Trump takes questions as he announced the creation of the "Trump-class" battleship during a statement to the media at Trump’s Mar-a-Lago estate on December 22, 2025, in Palm Beach, Florida. (Photo by Tasos Katopodis/Getty Images)
"In effect, an amnesty throws that out the window and says, well, we have these limits, but we're not going to enforce them," he continued.
TRUMP SAYS DEPORTATION PUSH HASN’T PUT 'SAME PRESSURE' ON FARMWORKERS, HOTEL STAFF: 'NOT EVEN CLOSE'

Drawing from the findings of a 2022 book called "Streets of Gold: America's Untold Story of Immigrant Success," Collins argued that today's immigrants are assimilating at a pace similar to that of immigrants of prior generations. America's current foreign-born population has matched a historic peak similar to late 1800s and early 1900s levels. About 15% of the current population is foreign-born.
The book, she said, compared people's memories of how their grandparents and great-grandparents assimilated when they came to the United States.
"And what they found was actually that immigrants are integrating it pretty much the same rates," she said.
She also said that work helps people to assimilate faster, and thus, if illegal immigrants were given the opportunity to work legally, assimilation would be a smoother process.

"I do think that one of the things America really is good at is us taking newcomers and turning them into Americans, and so I worry less about that" she said. "But I understand why there is a scenario where people could be afraid of that. But the data doesn't support it."
Fiscal Policy:

Camarota estimated that households headed by illegal immigrants receive approximately $50 billion annually in government benefits, often through programs for which their U.S.-born children are eligible. He cited Medicaid, Supplemental Security Income (SSI), Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) and free school lunches as examples, although illegal immigrants themselves are generally barred from receiving many federal welfare benefits.
TRUMP TELLS DHS CHIEF TO WORK WITH DEMOCRATS ON IMMIGRATION REFORM, BUT NO AMNESTY
Illegal immigrants use welfare not because they're lazy, but because most of them do not have educations higher than 11th grade level, Camarota said.

"Legalizing folks doesn't change the fact that the illegal population is overwhelmingly less educated, and less educated people just don't pay enough in taxes to cover their consumption of public services, especially when you consider all the means-tested programs they get," he said.
Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents conduct immigration enforcement operations in Minneapolis on Jan. 28, 2026. (Madison Thorn/Anadolu via Getty Images)
Low-income people, he noted, simply don't pay much in taxes.

"Remember, half of all workers pay no federal income tax," he said. "So, yes, illegal immigrants do pay taxes, and actually we think more than half already work on the books, so there's no big boon to taxpayers anyway. But now, they themselves will become eligible for welfare programs."

Collins conceded that while many immigrants have low education levels, he said that that doesn't mean all of them are working jobs that meet their education skills. She pointed to a 2013 Congressional Budget Office (CBO) analysis of the Gang of Eight's immigration bill, S. 744, which estimated that the legislation would increase federal tax revenues and reduce federal deficits by approximately $158 billion over 10 years, despite increased spending on government benefits.

"You get a little bit more tax revenue," she said. "They are potentially making higher wages, they're able to negotiate for different jobs and different wages because they have that legal work authorization," Collins said.
HISPANIC VOTERS ARE NATURAL CONSERVATIVES. REAGAN KNEW. GOP NEEDS TO PROVE IT AGAIN
She argued that with legal work authorization, some illegal immigrants would be able to fulfill their full potential in higher-level jobs.
Mark Krikorian runs CIS. He said that while thinking through the pros and cons of amnesty might be a useful thought exercise, the point is probably moot.

People wait inside a U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services office. The Trump administration issued a new rule allowing USCIS to refer certain asylum applications directly to immigration judges without first conducting an affirmative asylum interview. (John Moore/Getty Images)

"Well, to begin with, it's not going to happen," he said of an amnesty deal. The likelihood of anything happening, certainly until the Democrats come in, until the next Congress comes in, and even then, it is, in my opinion, close to zero."
For two reasons, Krikorian doesn't think Republicans have leverage to make a deal.
He says Democrats won't be willing to concede any restrictions on immigration, thus leaving Republicans with no incentive to make an amnesty deal for illegal immigrants.
HOUSE REPUBLICANS MOVE TO MAKE TRUMP'S BORDER POLICIES PERMANENT

He used DACA as an example. Recently, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin floated the possibility of a compromise involving DACA recipients — people who came to the United States as children and received temporary protections from deportation — that could give them permanent legal status.
"A DACA amnesty? Frankly, the DACAs already have amnesty. It's upgrading them from amnesty light to amnesty premium," he said.
He said the first Trump administration tried making a deal for tighter immigration measures using DACA recipients as a bargaining chip.
Pro-DACA protestors hold a march outside the U.S. Capitol Building calling for a pathway to citizenship on November 17, 2022, in Washington, D.C. (Nathan Posner/Anadolu Agency via Getty Images)

"That idea is valuable and could be productive, but there's no way that upgrading the DACA who already have Social Security numbers and work permits to regular green card status is something that the Democrats would give anything in exchange for," he said.

But Krikorian warned that giving green cards to DACA recipients could eventually allow them to sponsor additional relatives, including their parents, once they become U.S. citizens, although existing immigration restrictions could prevent some relatives from obtaining legal status.

"And that would have some effects, because once you have a green card, you can petition for certain relatives, and the five-year clock for citizenship starts," he said. "And when you become a citizen, you could then petition for your parents. There's no numerical caps for that."
Trump discussed on "60 Minutes" potentially working out a deal that would allow some illegal immigrants working in industries like hospitality and landscaping to remain in the country.

"When you go into a hotel, and you have a woman that's working there as a maid, as a cleaner as a this, as a that, as a waitress, a lot of good things, great jobs, and all of a sudden they're being taken out of the country, it's tough. It's a tough thing," Trump said on "60 Minutes."

Federal agents patrol the halls of immigration court at the Jacob K. Javitz Federal Building on July 8, 2025, in New York City. Various council members and a state senator attended immigration hearings and observed Immigration and Customs Enforcement as they continued their stepped-up tactics of detaining people during routine check-ins or showing up to court for their immigration hearings. (Spencer Platt/Getty Images)
MULLIN VOWS ‘ZERO CHANGE’ ON IMMIGRATION AFTER REPUBLICANS SUFFER CRUSHING MIDTERM LOSSES
He added that people whom he described as "far-right" want deportations regardless of whether the illegal immigrant is working.

The White House, meanwhile, says Trump's "strong immigration policy remains unchanged," and White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis told Fox News Digital that Democrats should work with the president to keep the border secure, remove dangerous criminal illegal immigrants from the country and stop drug trafficking.
She said the president's "commonsense immigration agenda" has resulted in the "most secure border in history."
SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER
"If Democrats choose to pursue radical left open border and mass amnesty policies, they are choosing to work against the interests of the American people," she said.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The Department of Homeland Security did not return a request for comment.
Peter D'Abrosca is a politics reporter at Fox News Digital.

title: Trump tangles with reporter on beautifying White House: ‘You’re so pathetic’
summary: President Donald Trump fired back at reporters over White House renovations and denied responsibility for the FAA's first full nationwide ground stop since 9/11.
story: Before departing for Asia Monday, President Donald Trump tangled with a reporter who pressed him on White House construction projects.

President Donald Trump beat back questions from reporters Monday morning suggesting he was spending too much time on making improvements to the White House while the Federal Aviation Administration struggled with remaking its outdated communication systems.
"You're so pathetic," Trump told a reporter when asked about the management of his time.
"I have a responsibility to make sure the symbol of our country is in decent shape," Trump said, noting he spends "very little time" on beautification projects.
"It takes me 10 minutes a day."
MONDAY TRAVEL FACES KEY TEST AS POSSIBLE CULPRIT IDENTIFIED BEHIND HISTORIC GROUND STOP
President Donald Trump talks to reporters while departing the White House on Nov. 16, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images)

As the reporter attempted to interject regarding federal funding priorities for the aviation system, Trump dismissed the cost of the White House repairs as "peanuts," asserting that he pays for the upgrades himself and trading personal barbs with the journalist.
"This doesn’t cost money," Trump said. "This is peanuts. This is called talent. Talent. You don’t have talent, you know. You don’t know what you don’t know."

When pressed later in the gaggle if he bears "responsibility" for the FAA's nationwide ground stop Friday night, the first full stoppage of flights since 9/11, Trump fired back and expressed support for Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy.
WHITE HOUSE SEIZES ON DELAYED OBAMA PRESIDENTIAL CENTER OPENING TO CROWN TRUMP ‘BUILDER-IN-CHIEF’
"I don't take any responsibility," Trump said. "They did a great job, Secretary Duffy. They acted incredibly. Everybody was safe. Nobody was hurt. No crashes, no nothing."
Trump also repeated placing the blame on Congress for failing to pass the necessary funding to upgrade the FAA's telecommunications system to modernize the U.S. airline infrastructure.

"I've already informed Congress, you know, we've been working with Congress to try and get the money," Trump said. "I think the one good thing that comes out of it, I'm sure Congress will now give us the money to fix [it].
"We want to have the best system in the world, and for that, we need Congress," he continued. "We've been trying to get the money for two years to fix it."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The fixes from copper to fiber optics are long overdue, Trump stressed.
"For 40 years, they should have done this with this system that's probably, on average, 50 years old," he concluded.

Eric Mack is a breaking news reporter and writer Sunday through Thursday, 6 a.m. ET to 2 p.m. ET, with a particular interest in stories that lead the news cycle on politics, elections, foreign affairs and government.

title: Historic GOP defeat fuels 11th-hour power struggle as new allies rally to rein in incoming Dem governor
summary: Texas state Rep. Brian Harrison says a historic conservative coalition is demanding Greg Abbott convene a special session before Democrats take over.
story: Gina Hinajosa plans to use emergency powers in the Lone Star State to lock energy prices in place, raising alarm from Nick Loris, president of a free-market advocacy group.

With Democrats poised to take control of the Texas governor's mansion for the first time in decades, Republican state Rep. Brian Harrison is rallying a coalition of conservative organizations behind a last-ditch push to rein in the sweeping emergency powers Gov. Greg Abbott has wielded for years.

"The largest coalition of conservative organizations ever formed to restore separation of powers and rein in unconstitutional emergency powers joins the call for [Republican Texas Gov. Greg Abbott] to convene a special session before Democrats take over!!" Harrison wrote in a statement posted on X on Thursday.

"I'm proud to be leading this effort (something I've been working on for many years on a bipartisan basis), and am grateful to [Citizens for Renewing America] for helping organize this unprecedented coalition fighting to limit the damage that Democrats can inflict on Texas if we don't act now!" he added.
The announcement comes after Harrison urged Abbott on Nov. 4 to call a special session to curb gubernatorial emergency powers in the state before Democratic Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa assumes office.
AMERICA SAW THE BLUE WAVE COMING — BUT DRASTICALLY UNDERESTIMATED THE EXTENT OF THE DEM TSUNAMI
Gina Hinojosa speaks to members of the media during a block walk campaign event in San Antonio, Texas, on Nov. 1, 2026. (Christopher Lee/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

"In her first national TV appearance after winning, Gina Hinojosa agreed with me that these powers can be abused," Harrison told Fox News Digital on Friday. "I renew my invitation for her to join my call to limit them immediately, as she’s told me she wants to for years."

"I will not sit silently and let Democrats turn Texas into a sanctuary state or enact socialist price controls without fighting back," the Texas Republican added. "I’m proud to provide the type of bold, pro-liberty leadership Texans deserve and honored to partner with an overwhelming and historic number of conservatives unifying in the call for action. Republicans are still in charge for months. Voters soundly rejected do-nothing Republicans, and any elected Republican advocating inaction is derelict in their duty to protect Texas."
Hinojosa told MS NOW in a Nov. 5 interview that "there's no question Greg Abbott has used his emergency powers in a way that is abusive."

"He has delivered a billion dollars in no-bid contracts to his donors," Hinojosa said. "My commitment is that I will only use emergency powers to deliver to the people of Texas at a time when Texans want relief, and I would hope no legislator would block that effort towards relief."
Hinojosa's campaign and Abbott's office did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Harrison said the "growing" list of groups supporting his calls for a special legislative session includes True Texas Project, Citizens for Renewing America, Texas Gun Rights and Gun Owners of America, among several others.
Citizens for Renewing America and Texas Gun Rights did not respond to Fox News Digital's request seeking comment.

"Gun Owners of America supports Representative Brian Harrison’s call for a special session to rein in the governor’s emergency powers," Gun Owners of America Texas State Director Leigh Gibson told Fox News Digital on Monday. "GOA has a proven track record of fighting executive overreach, including our successful efforts in 2021 to eliminate the governor’s authority to restrict firearms and ammunition."
Gov. Greg Abbott speaks during the Conservative Political Action Conference (CPAC) in Grapevine, Texas, on March 27, 2026. (Shelby Tauber/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

"True Texas Project has supported the call to rein in the governor's emergency powers since COVID, when Gov. Abbott used extremely poor judgment in shutting our state down and stealing individual liberties," True Texas Project CEO Julie McCarty told Fox News Digital on Friday. "Now here we are at the 11th hour, scrambling to do what should have been done  years ago."

"Folks are saying it's too late, it can't be done, and it would be a waste of money to try," McCarty added. "They aren't wrong. So yes, we support the effort, but we're also aware it will not happen. It's simply another failure that falls at Abbott's feet and gives a perfect example why so few could get behind his re-election campaign."
Harrison asserted Friday in a social media post that "this is what actual conservative UNITY looks like!"
TED CRUZ SAYS 'BLUE TSUNAMI' TOOK OVER TEXAS AFTER DEMOCRATS SWEPT STATEWIDE RACES
Republican Kentucky Sen. Rand Paul wrote in a Nov. 8 X post that he agrees "completely" with Harrison's call for a special legislative session to rein in gubernatorial emergency powers.
"Texas GOP should eliminate governor’s emergency powers," Paul said in the post.

Republican Texas state Rep. Wes Virdell recently told Nexstar that calling a lame-duck special legislative session would be a "guaranteed failure" if Democrats failed to show up, potentially leaving the House short of the 100 members required to conduct business under the Texas Constitution.

"It is one thing to pursue this if there was even a small chance of victory, but in my opinion this is guaranteed failure," Virdell told Nexstar in a statement. "This reminds me of running straight [into] a wall at full speed with no helmet and hoping for success. If Brian can produce a list of 15 or more Democrats that will show up so we can have [a] quorum, then count me in."

Harrison acknowledged on Nov. 12 that no other state lawmakers had joined his coalition yet, but noted that Republican Texas Rep. Chip Roy and Paul had expressed support for the effort, Texas Scorecard reported.
State Rep. Gina Hinojosa, then-gubernatorial candidate, speaks during a campaign event in Austin, Texas, on Nov. 2, 2026. (Jordan Vonderhaar/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
TEXAS DEMOCRATS PUT DEI BACK ON AGENDA AFTER SWEEPING TO POWER

Texas' governor has the ability to sign or veto bills passed by the state's Legislature, serve as commander in chief of the state's military forces and convene special sessions "for specific purposes," per Abbott's office.

Hinojosa vowed on the campaign trail that she plans to declare "a high-cost emergency" in Texas and issue executive orders to suspend the state's gas and diesel taxes and freeze residential electricity rates, the Texas Tribune reported on Nov. 4, though legal experts have questioned whether the governor has the authority to impose such a freeze.
TEXAS SENATE VICTOR JAMES TALARICO LAYS OUT COMMON GROUND WITH TRUMP, VOWS TO 'WORK TOGETHER'

"Greg Abbott needs to use his emergency powers to suspend the state gas tax," she wrote in an April 24, 2026, X post. "While working Texans are struggling to afford the basics, he can give immediate relief."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Hinojosa is poised to take office in January 2027. Abbott has not yet announced plans to call a special legislative session before Hinojosa assumes office.

title: Dem eyeing Homeland Security committee's oversight subcommittee gavel aims 'to dismantle DHS from the inside'
summary: A Democrat seeking the chairmanship of the House Homeland Security Committee's Oversight, Investigations and Accountability Subcommittee, wants "to dismantle DHS from the inside."
story: Rep. Brandon Gill, R-Texas, criticizes Rep. Delia Ramirez's, D-Ill., proposed legislation to abolish I.C.E. and CBP and replace DHS, calling the 'reimagining safety' policy dangerous, on 'The Will Cain Show.'

A Democrat, who noted that she is seeking the House Homeland Security Committee's Oversight, Investigations and Accountability Subcommittee chair, said that she aims "to dismantle" the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) "from the inside."

"I introduced a bill to dismantle DHS, and I intend to dismantle DHS from the inside. Every investigation we do — whether it’s about detention, who is profiting at the expense of children who are literally in cages, or the expansion of these 287(g) agreements where local police [work] with federal agents to hunt down people — is critical to provide the evidence necessary to be able to bring the most justice," she said Tuesday to Mother Jones, which noted that the discussion with the lawmaker had been edited for the sake of length and clarity.

Ramirez reportedly said that "there’s no other agency that has consolidated the amount of power that DHS has with the amount of money that DHS has in order to terrorize the American people and literally rob us from our civil rights, while at the same time saying that they’re doing it under the guise of protecting us from terrorism. There is no democracy if DHS continues to operate the way it does."
'SQUAD' DEMOCRAT FORMALLY INTRODUCES BILL TO ABOLISH ICE, BORDER PATROL AND DISMANTLE DHS

Rep. Delia Ramirez, D-Ill., holds signs as President Donald Trump delivered his address to a joint session of Congress in the House Chamber of the U.S. Capitol on Tuesday, March 4, 2025. (Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images)

"For me, investigations must lead into reimagining something new, where we protect cybersecurity infrastructure, where we protect FEMA, where we protect TSA, where we protect the customs functions at the border, and where we abolish ICE and CBP and reinvest funds towards healthcare, community safety and first responders," she said, according to the report.
Ramirez, who has served in the House since early 2023, just won re-election during the 2026 midterms.
Democrats will have the majorities in both chambers of Congress next year, and the congresswoman noted to Mother Jones that she is "pursuing the Homeland Security Oversight Subcommittee gavel."
'SQUAD' DEMOCRAT SLAMMED BY TRUMP ADMIN FOR MOST 'RADICAL' PLAN TARGETING ICE YET

Rep. Delia Ramirez, D-Ill., speaks during the People's State Of The Union Rally And Boycott Outside The Capitol on the National Mall on Feb. 24, 2026 in Washington, D.C. (Jemal Countess/Getty Images for MoveOn)

She asserted that "there is no affordability without accountability. Point-blank. If you want to actually talk about why people are living and experiencing the challenges they are right now, whether it’s that they can’t afford to buy groceries, they can’t afford to drive to work or pick up their kids, or they can’t afford the rent or buy their home, or why they’re living in the shadows and their businesses are shutting down, there has to be accountability to the actors that have made that happen. And it also means accountability to those that have terrorized them," she told the outlet.

"Yes, we should be passing Medicare for All. Yes, we need to pass a bill that increases wages in this country. Yes, we should abolish super PACs and tax the rich. But we also have to understand that, as we fight for an affordable country, we have to hold every fascist in this administration accountable," Ramirez added.
DEMS PIVOT FROM 'AFFORDABILITY' PITCH TO DHS PROBE THREATS AFTER MIDTERM WINS
