title: U.S. loses measles-elimination status, erasing decades of progress
summary: Measles is no longer eliminated in the U.S., a United Nations commission determined, reversing one of the country’s greatest public health achievements this century.
story: Measles is no longer eliminated in the United States, reversing one of the country’s greatest public health achievements this century.

An independent commission of the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), a group within the World Health Organization, revoked the U.S.’s measles-elimination status, according to sources familiar with the vote, after determining that the virus has circulated nonstop for more than a year.
The U.S. earned the designation in 2000. Now, measles is once again endemic.
PAHO is expected to officially announce its decision on Tuesday.

“The United States has an extraordinary measles problem. We’ve had more measles cases in the last 18 months than we’ve had in the previous 25 years combined,” said Noel Brewer, a public health professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill.
Upwards of 5,400 cases have been recorded this year — more than double last year’s count and the highest since 1991. Ten people have died, according to state health departments.

title: United Airlines says it has resolved a ‘widespread system outage’
summary: United Airlines on Monday said a widespread system outage that delayed flight departures is over.
story: United Airlines on Monday said a widespread system outage that delayed flight departures is over.
In a statement early Monday evening, the airline said it had resolved a technology issue linked to the problem, which came on the heels of a nationwide FAA ground stop.
While some flights were delayed, the company said, there was no impact on flights in progress or on United Express flights.
United announced the outage roughly an hour earlier, just before 5 p.m.

The union representing United pilots said in a statement that the outage had affected multiple pilot-facing applications, including crew communications and messaging systems, as well as the airline’s ability to provide final aircraft weight information for departing flights.

The union said it was working with management to better understand the scope of the disruption. Pilots had been advised to follow procedures in the flight operations manual, according to the statement.

A passenger on a United flight bound for Hong Kong told NBC News that a pilot announced that they’d been unable to get performance data for takeoff because of an IT issue. The pilot said they planned on doing “old school” calculations so they could take off, according to the passenger, Halina Eth.
In another announcement, the pilot said that systems were back online and there was a “very narrow window of opportunity to get this flight in the air,” according to a video shared with NBC News.
The issue did not appear to be related to technical issues that prompted the ground stop that halted air travel across the United States for more than four hours Friday evening.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Other airlines did not appear to be affected by Monday’s United issue.

It’s the latest system relied on by millions of Americans to falter. Earlier Monday, JPMorganChase said a technical issue was causing some banking transactions to be delayed for both its own customers and others.

Late Friday, the FAA was forced to issue a nationwide ground stop after a fiber upgrade crashed a critical communication system. By Monday, air travel in the U.S. was largely returning to normal after a chaotic weekend for travelers, crews and airlines.
And last week, Microsoft Outlook went down due to what the tech giant said was a “bug” and overwhelmed servers.

While there is no evidence that any of the issues are related, they seem to be fulfilling concerns about America’s overreliance on aging infrastructure. They’re also occurring against a backdrop of warnings about AI risks and cyberattacks, stoking fears that wider problems may be afoot.

title: The FAA ground stop left them stranded, so they bought a car and drove it home
summary: A nationwide ground stop left Tara Harding and her employees stranded. Striking out on planes and trains, she opted to just buy an automobile.
story: Tara Harding and her employees were at the airport trying to get home from a work trip when a nationwide ground stop left them stranded in Charlotte, North Carolina — roughly 1,600 miles from home in Bismarck, North Dakota.
She found a $48,000 solution in the form of a new Ford Bronco.

Travelers across the U.S. were left scrambling Friday when the Federal Aviation Administration announced that it was grounding all flights as it saw inconsistencies in radar data and communications. Officials said that 20,000 flights were affected in the hourslong ground stop, with 12,000 “unable to recover” after the order lifted. Thousands more flights were either delayed or canceled the next day as airlines scrambled to recover service.

Harding, a nurse practitioner who owns a clinic, was ready to get home Friday after being in town for a training with two of her employees. Her group had been at the airport for about 30 minutes when the ground stop occurred.
All three women started out trying to find options through Delta Air Lines, but flights were delayed and rebooked until they gave up the idea of getting in the air altogether, Harding said.

“In the midst of all of that, though, we’re like, ‘We should probably look at trying to get a rental car,’” Harding said. “So we were trying to look, all three of us at one time, trying to get a rental car. There was zero available rental cars within a four-hour radius.”
Greyhound? Sold out.
Amtrak? No luck.
Uber? No rides to Bismarck.
Overwhelmed and out of ideas, Harding called her husband to ask what she should do. He relayed to her an idea from his mom.
“She said, ‘Why don’t you guys go buy a car?’” Harding recalled.
At that point, the women had been trying unsuccessfully to rebook their flights or find alternatives for more than an hour.

So they started texting with a sales agent at a Ford dealership who promised to stay open while they waited 30 minutes for an Uber out of the Charlotte Douglas International Airport. They arrived at 7:45 p.m. and left with a new Bronco less than two hours later.
Harding said the process gave her an adrenaline rush.
“When we were leaving the airport, I was three-way calling with my husband, the car dealer and my employees, and we were looking at each other like, ‘Is this really happening right now?’” she said.
Harding said she knows it sounds “insane,” but she did what she had to do, relying on a problem-solving instinct she tied to being both an entrepreneur and a nurse.
“If it was just me, it would have probably been different,” she said. “But I had two employees that needed to get home to their children, and we had patients on Monday morning.”

title: Robert Pattinson named as the newest James Bond
summary: Actor Robert Pattinson has been tapped to take on the role of James Bond as Amazon MGM Studios seeks to continue the blockbuster film franchise.
story: Agent 007 has a new face.
Actor Robert Pattinson has been tapped to take on the role of James Bond as Amazon MGM Studios seeks to continue the blockbuster film franchise.

The studio announced the “Twilight” and “The Batman” alum as its choice to pick up the secret agent mantle, making the 40-year-old the latest in a list of leading men who have had the honor of playing the spy.

“James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime,” Pattinson said in a statement, adding, “To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement.”
The news comes after years of speculation over who would take over the role after Daniel Craig announced in 2019 that he was leaving the franchise.
In the last week, rumors over Craig’s successor centered on Pattinson after a report from Puck suggested he was the front-runner.

Denis Villeneuve is directing the new Bond film, which further fueled the speculation given that Pattinson collaborated with Villeneuve on the “Dune” franchise. The third installment of that franchise hits theaters in December.

From starring in A24’s indie film “The Drama” to blockbuster epic “The Odyssey,” Pattinson has had a massive year, joining the handful of Hollywood stars who have dominated the big screen. Most recently, he starred as “Dateline NBC” alum Chris Hansen in “Primetime,” the A24 film that follows the TV personality’s “To Catch a Predator” era.
The script for the new Bond film is being written by Steven Knight, who created the TV series “Peaky Blinders.”

Amazon MGM Studios, the tech giant’s film unit, took over “creative control” of the James Bond series under a new deal with the franchise’s longtime producers, Michael G. Wilson and Barbara Broccoli. The deal was announced in February 2025.
Now, “Spider-Man” producer Amy Pascal and “Harry Potter”  producer David Heyman will take on the latest installment, producing through Pascal Pictures and Heyday Films.
In a statement, Mike Hopkins, head of Prime Video and Amazon MGM Studios, emphasized that Pattinson’s casting is helping to “usher in a new era of Bond.”

“This iconic character has captivated audiences around the world for more than six decades, and there’s no doubt that Robert’s remarkable range, magnetic screen presence, and quiet intensity make him an exceptional choice to carry that legacy forward,” he said, praising the “world-class creative team in place” that will be carrying on the franchise’s legacy.

Bond fans have had many thoughts as to who would take on the mantle, with many hoping that Idris Elba would be tapped as the next British super spy. But Elba told People magazine in August that he was never truly in the race to become the next Bond.
In recent months, Jack Lowden, Josh O’Connor and Callum Turner reportedly also tested for the role.

Bond has evolved into one of the most coveted roles for male actors in the United Kingdom. The book-to-screen character written by Ian Fleming has had a unique staying power across generations, beginning with Sean Connery in the 1962 film “Dr. No.” The Scottish actor played Bond across seven films and two decades.

George Lazenby, the only Australian to play Bond, starred in 1969’s “On Her Majesty’s Secret Service.” He only played Bond for that film, which some have called one of the most underrated. Among the film’s fans is director Christopher Nolan, who called it his favorite of the franchise.

But it was Roger Moore who was considered to be the one who replaced Connery in the iconic spy franchise. Moore was often criticized in comparison to Connery, but he was chosen to star in seven of the franchise’s movies.

After Moore’s final Bond film in 1985, actor Timothy Dalton was given a smaller stint as the British agent. Dalton starred in two films, including “Licence to Kill,” in which he chose to portray Bond with a darker, more serious tone than previously seen by fans.

The character took another turn when Pierce Brosnan was given the role. Brosnan said he grew up adoring both Connery and Moore in the role, telling GQ in 2014 that it never felt “real” to him that he held the job.
Brosnan was told following his final Bond film, “Die Another Day,” that the character was being rethought and negotiations with his agent to continue his role had stopped.

“And that certainly dug into the solar plexus of life, just because it was pretty gut-wrenching and because it had been somewhat heralded that I was coming back,” the Irishman told GQ. “So, it’s just business. And you’re the one caught in the crosshairs.”
Brosnan was replaced by Craig, who was lauded by critics and fans alike after he made his 007 debut in the franchise’s “Casino Royale” installment.

The actor chose to leave the fictional spy life behind after five films, saying on “The Graham Norton Show” in 2021 that he was glad to be leaving on his own terms even though it was an emotional decision.
“I’m grateful to the producers for allowing me to do that,” Craig said. “But I shall miss it. I’ll probably be incredibly bitter when the new person takes over.”
In a statement posted to X, Ian Fleming Publications, which owns and manages the literary rights to James Bond, praised the casting news.

“As Bond himself reflects at the end of Moonraker when facing the fact that the object of his affections is engaged to another man, ‘He must play the role which she expected of him. The tough man of the world. The Secret Agent. The man who was only a silhouette.’ We look forward to Pattinson stepping into that silhouette and making it his own,” the account wrote. “We have no doubt that Ian Fleming would be amazed at the longevity of his creation and the fact that the world is still hungry for tales of the world’s greatest spy.​”
Lazenby also posted a congratulatory video message for Pattinson on X, saying “Robert, welcome to the most exclusive club in the world. But remember to enjoy yourself.”
Online, many diehard Pattinson fans — particularly millennials who identified as “Twihards” — were thrilled by the star’s newest role.
“A great day for us Team Edward girlies,” wrote one X user, referring to Pattinson’s role as brooding, telepathic vampire Edward Cullen.

Several users even posted a scene from the first “Twilight” film, released in 2008, in which Pattinson’s Edward is seen opening the car door for his romantic interest Bella Swan (Kristen Stewart) after one of their peers announces the school dance theme is Monte Carlo.
“Gambling, tuxedos and Bond, James Bond,” one of the characters says, before it cuts to Pattinson and Stewart.
“Twilight literally predicted Robert Pattinson being James Bond btw,” wrote one X user who shared the clip.
Within minutes after the news dropped, many had also already cut thirsty fan edits compiling clips of the actor in his various roles and appearances.
But there were many who blasted the choice. “robert pattinson as bond is such a boring choice man, please for the love of god choose an unknown,” one X user noted.
And others who worried that Pattinson will be too busy with Bond for other roles.
“we’re never getting that second Batman movie…” wrote one X user.
“He’ll do great, I’m sure of it,” wrote another user. “But man am I still disappointed.”

title: Grammys 2027 nominees: Raye, Rosalía and women artists dominate major categories
summary: RAYE, Rosalía and women artists dominate Grammy 2027 nominees list
story: Baby, where the hell is her Grammy?

Female artists led the 2027 Grammy nominee list, which was unveiled during an early morning livestream Monday. The nominees were announced by a star-studded lineup of past Grammy winners and nominees, including Alan Menken, David Guetta and Pharrell Williams.
Nominees across 100 categories were selected by 16,000 voting members of the Recording Academy. Eligible artists released their music during the period encompassing Aug. 31, 2025 — Aug. 28, 2026.
The 69th Grammy Awards will take place at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles on Feb. 7. The show will air on ABC and stream on Disney+ and Hulu.
Here are some of the key takeaways from this year’s announcement.
Raye and Rosalía lead nominees

British singer-songwriter Raye came out on top with a whopping 11 nominations, including for song, record and album of the year. The 28-year-old rose to the top of the charts this year with her hit, “Where Is My Husband!” She now joins Beyoncé in tying the record for the most nods earned by a female artist in a single  year.

Rosalía, who recently made history at the Latin Grammys by becoming the first female artist to win album of the year three times, snagged nine nominations. “LUX,” her fourth full-length album, features 13 different languages.

Olivia Rodrigo snagged seven nods for her latest album “you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love.” Phoebe Bridges, Ella Langley and collaborator Miranda Lambert all also earned seven nominations apiece.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Leaving space for ‘Wicked’
It may feel like an eternity ago that “Wicked: For Good” was released in theaters.

But Cynthia Erivo and Ariana Grande notched a best traditional pop vocal performance nomination for their song “For Good,” from the sequel to the 2024 Broadway adaptation about an unlikely friendship between two witches.
Erivo starred as the Wicked Witch of the West and Grande as the Good Witch, Glinda in the Universal Pictures film. (NBC News and Universal Pictures share Comcast as a parent company.)
Erivo and Grande are no strangers to the Grammys, having won two Grammys and three Grammys, respectively.
The film was also nominated in the best score soundtrack for visual media and best song written for visual media categories
Dolly Parton receives posthumous nods
The “Queen of Country” music, who died at age 80 in August, was among the nominees in the best country duo and group performance categories.
Parton will also likely be heavily featured in the annual emotional in memoriam segment.
Beyoncé earns her 100th Grammy nomination
Queen Bey made history Monday with her 100th Grammy nomination for best R&B solo performance for her song, “MORNING DEW (DONK).”
Beyoncé has won 35 Grammys in her storied career — the most of any female artist.
Taylor Swift’s recognized for ‘Showgirl’ and ‘Toy Story’
Yes, Swift’s 12th album, “The Life of a Showgirl” came out over a year ago, and yes it still earned several nominations Monday morning.

“Showgirl” took a spot in two of the three top categories, with lead single “The Fate of Ophelia,” earning a place for record of the year, and the album making the list of potential album of the year winners — an award Swift has won more than any other artist in her 20-year career.
“Showgirl” also nabbed nominations for best remixed recording of “Opalite,” and for best pop duo/group performance for song “The Life of a Showgirl,” which features Sabrina Carpenter.
The album, however, did not rise to a nomination for best pop vocal album.
Swift also got two nominations for her single “I Knew It I Knew You,” which she wrote for “Toy Story 5” and released in June — including song of the year.
Swift on Monday tied for the most song of the year nominations, with nine total throughout her career, including hits like “You Belong With Me,” “Blank Space” and “Anti-Hero.”
Madonna makes a comeback
Madonna received her first nominations in 16 years, since 2010, with “Bring Your Love.”
The pop icon, 68, has won 7 Grammy Awards in her decades-long career.
This year marked a comeback for the artist, who also performed at the MTV Video Music Awards for the first time in 23 years. There, she also took home three awards, including artist of the year.
Oscar buzz starts now
The best score soundtrack for visual media (includes film and TV) is typically stacked with Oscar contenders. This year was no different.
Six-time Grammy-winning composer Ludwig Göransson scored two more nods Monday, for his work on two films: “The Odyssey” and “Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu.”
Göransson has won three Oscars and is expected to be nominated again at Hollywood’s biggest night.
Universal’s “The Odyssey,” which kicked off its Oscar campaign last week, is an expected front-runner in several categories for the Academy Awards.

Daniel Pemberton’s “Project Hail Mary” score was also recognized. The Amazon MGM Studios film, which stars Ryan Gosling, is also among the buzzy Oscar contenders. The Grammy nomination marks a first for Pemberton.
The score for “One Battle After Another,” from composer Jonny Greenwood, was also in the mix of this year’s nominees. The film won six Oscars at the 2026 Oscars.

Swift’s “Toy Story” single, which received Recording Academy recognition, is also expected to be nominated at the Oscars next year. The pop star has already been busy campaigning for the song, with the Grammy nominations now helping fuel her to the top of the contender list.

title: Somali Uber driver left with life-threatening injuries as police investigate possible hate crime
summary: An Uber driver was “fighting for his life” Monday following an attack that Minnesota police are investigating as a potential hate crime against the Somali American man, authorities said.
story: An Uber driver was “fighting for his life” Monday following an attack that Minnesota police are investigating as a potential hate crime against the Somali American man, authorities said.

The driver was a “victim of a serious assault” on Saturday, leaving him with “life-threatening injuries that investigators believe were inflicted by a passenger in the vehicle,” according to a Hopkins police statement.
Hopkins is a city in Hennepin County, just outside Minneapolis.
“Investigators are examining all available evidence and considering all potential motives, including whether bias played a role in the assault,” Hopkins Police Chief Brent Johnson said.
Police did not immediately identify the driver.
The Minnesota chapter of the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR) and the victim’s family identified him as Somali American Mohamed Yusuf.
“A passenger asked his name, told him he didn’t like that name and then he attacked him,” said Suleiman Adan, deputy executive director of CAIR Minnesota.
For Subscribers
The attacker tried to strangle the driver and then used the victim’s car to try running over him, according to Jaylani Hussein, executive director of CAIR Minnesota.
“This is one of the most heinous attacks that we have ever seen,”  Hussein said.

Uber said it was shocked by the attack. “We banned the rider from the Uber platform and are keeping the driver and his loved ones in our thoughts as we continue to support law enforcement with their investigation,” the company said in a statement.
Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison reposted a Somali news story identifying the victim with a picture of him in the hospital.
For Subscribers

“There will be accountability for this horrific crime,” Ellison added. “My heart breaks for Mohamed, his loved ones, and our Somali and Muslim communities apparently targeted by this assault. Everyone should feel safe and be safe in Minnesota — no exceptions. Hate and violence have no place here.”
Minnesota has become a hub for Somali immigration, and President Donald Trump has told Minnesotans to “fight back” against this community of recently arrived Americans.

The president has repeatedly verbally attacked Somalis, as well as Rep. Ilhan Omar, who was born in Somalia. Federal agents searched the lawmaker’s home last month in an inquiry of possible irregularities in her immigration process. Omar has denied any allegations and said she feels “confident in my truth.”

Trump’s attacks on Somali immigrants in Minnesota come in the wake of reports last year about dozens of people of Somali descent who were convicted of fraud schemes. Since then, Trump has called Somalis “crooks” and referred to Somalia as “filthy, dirty, disgusting, dirty.”
Somali immigrants are living in “fear, hatred, bigotry and demonization” that’s “come from the highest office of the land,” according to Hussein.
“This rhetoric has built an environment that we are living in today, an environment which we believe has created this heinous attack that took place on Saturday night here in Minnesota,” he added.
Hopkins Mayor Patrick Hanlon asked the public for time to allow department investigators to do their work.

“We ask for the community’s patience and understanding as investigators work diligently to determine the full circumstances surrounding this case,” the mayor said. “All of our investigators have been working non-stop to follow up on evidence and determine the facts.”

title: GOP Rep. James Comer announces bid for Kentucky governor
summary: Rep. James Comer, R-Ky., announced Monday night that he is running for governor of Kentucky in an attempt to flip the governor’s mansion from blue to red in 2027.
story: Rep. James Comer, R-Ky., announced Monday night that he is running for governor of Kentucky in an attempt to flip the governor’s mansion from blue to red in 2027.
The Republican congressman’s announcement comes on the heels this month’s blue tsunami that swept Democrats into control of both chambers of Congress.
Democratic Gov. Andy Beshear, who is term limited, has led Kentucky since 2019, though voters backed Republicans for statewide positions in the midterm elections.

Comer announced his candidacy in a tele-town hall, where he took questions from callers. While answering one of the questions, the congressman sought to create some distance from President Donald Trump.

“I think that some of the things the president has tried to do on the national level had good intentions, but there are always unintended consequences,” said Comer, who like many House Republicans aligned himself with Trump over the years.
Comer was first elected to Congress in 2016. He currently serves as chair of the House Oversight Committee, which oversaw Congress’ probe into Jeffrey Epstein.

Kentucky is one of the few states to have off-year elections for governor — the others are Louisiana and Mississippi. The 2027 election could be an early test of how durable the blue wave will prove one year out from the midterm elections — and a year before the 2028 presidential election.
For Subscribers
Trump won Kentucky by more than 30 percentage points in 2024, and Comer won re-election this year by an even wider margin, defeating his Democratic opponent by more than 35 points.
For Subscribers

Comer is the biggest name to jump into the race on the GOP side. Three other Republicans have declared their intentions to run, including former reality TV contestant Charles “Bruiser” Martin and Rick Hardin, a state attorney.
On the Democratic side, Lt. Gov. Jacqueline Coleman and former Beshear senior adviser Rocky Adkins have said they are running.
Kentucky will hold its primaries on May 18.

title: U.S. loses measles-elimination status, erasing decades of progress
summary: Measles is no longer eliminated in the U.S., a United Nations commission determined, reversing one of the country’s greatest public health achievements this century.
story: Measles is no longer eliminated in the United States, reversing one of the country’s greatest public health achievements this century.

An independent commission of the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), a group within the World Health Organization, revoked the U.S.’s measles-elimination status, according to sources familiar with the vote, after determining that the virus has circulated nonstop for more than a year.
The U.S. earned the designation in 2000. Now, measles is once again endemic.
PAHO is expected to officially announce its decision on Tuesday.

“The United States has an extraordinary measles problem. We’ve had more measles cases in the last 18 months than we’ve had in the previous 25 years combined,” said Noel Brewer, a public health professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill.
Upwards of 5,400 cases have been recorded this year — more than double last year’s count and the highest since 1991. Ten people have died, according to state health departments.

title: One of the victims of the Washington, D.C., gym shooting is a gun control activist
summary: One of the people wounded in last week’s Washington, D.C., shooting is an anti-gun activist from Minnesota who was walking her daughter’s dog at the time, the daughter said Monday.
story: One of the people wounded in last week’s Washington, D.C., shooting is an anti-gun activist from Minnesota who was walking her daughter’s dog at the time, the daughter said Monday.
Susan Hamerski, 67, was shot in the temple. She is in stable condition and “past the life-threatening part, but she still has a long way to go,” her daughter, Madeleine Hamerski, said.
Hamerski was one of five people hit by gunfire on Thursday after disgruntled doctor Matt Wade Lambert, 55, fatally shot the manager of his condo building in a gym located on the ground floor.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
He then ran upstairs to his penthouse and began spraying bullets from his balcony at the people below, according to police. One of those bullets struck Hamerski.
Family friend Tina Wilcox, who is acting as the family’s spokesperson, said Hamerski’s injuries “are extensive.”
“Right now, she is unable to speak or swallow” and is breathing with the help of a ventilator, Wilcox said. “The bullet entered her temple and exited through her jaw and did a lot of damage.”
Hamerski will need multiple surgeries to restore function to her jaw and tongue, as well as reconstructive surgery to repair her face, Wilcox said.
“Then she’ll need months of rehabilitative therapy,” she said.
Hamerski worked for six years with the grassroots advocacy movement Moms Demand Action, which fights for public safety measures to protect communities from gun violence, her daughter said.
But the reason she was in Washington was that her daughter was on her honeymoon and she was dog-sitting the newlywed’s dog, Wrigley.
“She was walking Wrigley when she was shot,” her daughter said.
Law enforcement responded quickly to Thursday’s shooting, which took place in the trendy Logan Circle neighborhood, just a mile from the White House.
But by the time they arrived on the scene, Lambert had barricaded himself inside his condo and was shooting through the door, police said. He then fatally shot himself, officials said.

After she underwent surgery, and while recovering in the intensive care unit, Hamerski found the strength to write a brief note to her family in which she stressed her support for gun control, her daughter said.

“She was coming out of surgery and it came out kind of fuzzy, but the family knew what she was trying to say. ... The point being the gun violence is not simply a political issue, a criminal issue, or a matter of individual tragedy,” Wilcox said in a text message. “It’s also now a public health crisis because it’s happening so often.”
Previously, Hamerski worked for the Minnesota Department of Health and served on the board of the Illusion Theater in Minneapolis, her family said. She is also a poet.

title: United Airlines says it has resolved a ‘widespread system outage’
summary: United Airlines on Monday said a widespread system outage that delayed flight departures is over.
story: United Airlines on Monday said a widespread system outage that delayed flight departures is over.
In a statement early Monday evening, the airline said it had resolved a technology issue linked to the problem, which came on the heels of a nationwide FAA ground stop.
While some flights were delayed, the company said, there was no impact on flights in progress or on United Express flights.
United announced the outage roughly an hour earlier, just before 5 p.m.

The union representing United pilots said in a statement that the outage had affected multiple pilot-facing applications, including crew communications and messaging systems, as well as the airline’s ability to provide final aircraft weight information for departing flights.

The union said it was working with management to better understand the scope of the disruption. Pilots had been advised to follow procedures in the flight operations manual, according to the statement.

A passenger on a United flight bound for Hong Kong told NBC News that a pilot announced that they’d been unable to get performance data for takeoff because of an IT issue. The pilot said they planned on doing “old school” calculations so they could take off, according to the passenger, Halina Eth.
In another announcement, the pilot said that systems were back online and there was a “very narrow window of opportunity to get this flight in the air,” according to a video shared with NBC News.
The issue did not appear to be related to technical issues that prompted the ground stop that halted air travel across the United States for more than four hours Friday evening.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Other airlines did not appear to be affected by Monday’s United issue.

It’s the latest system relied on by millions of Americans to falter. Earlier Monday, JPMorganChase said a technical issue was causing some banking transactions to be delayed for both its own customers and others.

Late Friday, the FAA was forced to issue a nationwide ground stop after a fiber upgrade crashed a critical communication system. By Monday, air travel in the U.S. was largely returning to normal after a chaotic weekend for travelers, crews and airlines.
And last week, Microsoft Outlook went down due to what the tech giant said was a “bug” and overwhelmed servers.

While there is no evidence that any of the issues are related, they seem to be fulfilling concerns about America’s overreliance on aging infrastructure. They’re also occurring against a backdrop of warnings about AI risks and cyberattacks, stoking fears that wider problems may be afoot.

title: An early look at the 2028 Senate map: From the Politics Desk
summary: In today’s edition, Sahil Kapur dives into the next battle for the Senate.
story: Welcome to From the Politics Desk, a daily newsletter that brings you the NBC News Politics team’s latest reporting and analysis from the White House, Capitol Hill and the campaign trail.
In today’s edition, Sahil Kapur dives into the next battle for the Senate. Plus, Megan Brand explores how Black voters fueled the inroads Democrats made this year in the South.
— Adam Wollner
An early look at the 2028 Senate map
In one election night, Democrats turned a deep structural disadvantage in the Senate into an upper hand heading into the next presidential cycle.

After Republicans entered the year as favorites to maintain control, Democrats are now on pace to gain nine seats, with NBC News Decision Desk characterizing the Alaska Senate race as a likely victory for former Rep. Mary Pelotla. That would give the party a 56-44 majority, which would be the largest since 2009.
It also means the GOP would need to pick up at least six seats to flip control of the chamber in 2028 (and seven if they don’t control the vice presidency).
Here’s an early look at the 2028 Senate map.

Core battleground: There are six states that were decided by single digits in the last three presidential elections. That includes four Democratic-held seats in Arizona (Mark Kelly), Nevada (Catherine Cortez Masto), Georgia (Raphael Warnock) and Pennsylvania (John Fetterman).
Republicans will need to capture all four of those seats to give themselves a realistic shot at the majority in 2028.

Of the four Democrats, Fetterman faces the greatest danger of getting a primary challenger after his popularity with Democrats has plummeted. Kelly and Warnock are in the early 2028 presidential conversation; they’ll both have an important decision to make about whether to seek re-election or make a run for the White House.
There are also two Republican-held seats in this category: Wisconsin (Ron Johnson) and North Carolina (Ted Budd).
Johnson survived in 2022 by just 1 point while Budd won by 3 points in a midterm year in which Democrats were on the receiving end of backlash from voters with Joe Biden in the White House.
Extended battleground, red-state edition: There are six states President Donald Trump carried by double digits two years ago that became highly competitive in 2026.
For Subscribers

The first is Ohio, which Trump won by 11 points in 2024 and Democrat Sherrod Brown won by 5 points this year. Brown’s victory was a special election, so the seat is up again in 2028. It will mark the only double-digit Trump state represented by a Democrat in the next cycle.

The others include four Republican-held states where the other Senate seat flipped from red to blue this year: Iowa (Chuck Grassley), Kansas (Jerry Moran), South Carolina (Tim Scott) and, assuming Democrats officially prevail, Alaska (Lisa Murkowski).

Rounding out the list is Florida, where GOP Sen. Ashley Moody defeated underfunded progressive Democrat Angie Nixon by less than 3 points. Like Ohio, this was a special election, so Moody will have to run again in two years.
For Subscribers

Can lightning strike twice? Democrats needed a dream environment (and, in some cases, weak GOP candidates) to make those states competitive in 2026. It’s far from clear they can replicate that in two years. But if they can, a filibuster-proof majority of 60 seats could be within reach for Democrats.

Extended battleground, blue-state edition: If Republicans sweep every red and purple state mentioned above, they’ll have picked up five Democratic-held seats, needing at least one more to capture Senate control. That’s where blue-leaning territory comes into focus.
Judging by recent presidential elections, New Hampshire (Maggie Hassan) is probably the GOP’s best chance.
From there the hill gets much steeper, with seats up in the solidly Democratic states of California, Colorado, Connecticut, Hawaii, Illinois, Maryland, New York, Oregon, Vermont and Washington.

How difficult are those states? In 2022, Republicans zeroed in on Colorado and Washington as sleeper races after recruiting who they viewed as strong candidates. They ultimately lost both by double digits.

It’s almost a mirror image of the rough environment Democrats faced entering 2026 — they needed to win at least two solidly red states to have a shot at Senate control. Now it’s Republicans who would need to win at least one blue state to give themselves a chance.
How the tables have turned.
How a surge in Black turnout propelled Democrats in key Southern states

Black voters turned out in South Carolina at a level more similar to a presidential election year than a midterm year, according to state data, helping propel Sen.-elect Annie Andrews across the finish line in the longtime red state, while similar patterns powered other Democrats across the country.

Political experts and activists say higher Black voter turnout paved the way for Democrats to flip both the House and the Senate, with Democrats making gains in other traditionally red states with large Black populations, including Mississippi. Black voters played key roles in races in Georgia and Louisiana, too.

Running underneath it all, the activists told NBC News, was an undercurrent of anger and motivation stemming from redistricting efforts and the Supreme Court’s Louisiana v. Callais decision, which weakened the Voting Rights Act. The April decision kicked off redistricting efforts in some Republican-led states to cut Democratic seats where many Black voters live.

title: The FAA ground stop left them stranded, so they bought a car and drove it home
summary: A nationwide ground stop left Tara Harding and her employees stranded. Striking out on planes and trains, she opted to just buy an automobile.
story: Tara Harding and her employees were at the airport trying to get home from a work trip when a nationwide ground stop left them stranded in Charlotte, North Carolina — roughly 1,600 miles from home in Bismarck, North Dakota.
She found a $48,000 solution in the form of a new Ford Bronco.

Travelers across the U.S. were left scrambling Friday when the Federal Aviation Administration announced that it was grounding all flights as it saw inconsistencies in radar data and communications. Officials said that 20,000 flights were affected in the hourslong ground stop, with 12,000 “unable to recover” after the order lifted. Thousands more flights were either delayed or canceled the next day as airlines scrambled to recover service.

Harding, a nurse practitioner who owns a clinic, was ready to get home Friday after being in town for a training with two of her employees. Her group had been at the airport for about 30 minutes when the ground stop occurred.
All three women started out trying to find options through Delta Air Lines, but flights were delayed and rebooked until they gave up the idea of getting in the air altogether, Harding said.

“In the midst of all of that, though, we’re like, ‘We should probably look at trying to get a rental car,’” Harding said. “So we were trying to look, all three of us at one time, trying to get a rental car. There was zero available rental cars within a four-hour radius.”
Greyhound? Sold out.
Amtrak? No luck.
Uber? No rides to Bismarck.
Overwhelmed and out of ideas, Harding called her husband to ask what she should do. He relayed to her an idea from his mom.
“She said, ‘Why don’t you guys go buy a car?’” Harding recalled.
At that point, the women had been trying unsuccessfully to rebook their flights or find alternatives for more than an hour.

So they started texting with a sales agent at a Ford dealership who promised to stay open while they waited 30 minutes for an Uber out of the Charlotte Douglas International Airport. They arrived at 7:45 p.m. and left with a new Bronco less than two hours later.
Harding said the process gave her an adrenaline rush.
“When we were leaving the airport, I was three-way calling with my husband, the car dealer and my employees, and we were looking at each other like, ‘Is this really happening right now?’” she said.
Harding said she knows it sounds “insane,” but she did what she had to do, relying on a problem-solving instinct she tied to being both an entrepreneur and a nurse.
“If it was just me, it would have probably been different,” she said. “But I had two employees that needed to get home to their children, and we had patients on Monday morning.”

title: Somali Uber driver left with life-threatening injuries as police investigate possible hate crime
summary: An Uber driver was “fighting for his life” Monday following an attack that Minnesota police are investigating as a potential hate crime against the Somali American man, authorities said.
story: An Uber driver was “fighting for his life” Monday following an attack that Minnesota police are investigating as a potential hate crime against the Somali American man, authorities said.

The driver was a “victim of a serious assault” on Saturday, leaving him with “life-threatening injuries that investigators believe were inflicted by a passenger in the vehicle,” according to a Hopkins police statement.
Hopkins is a city in Hennepin County, just outside Minneapolis.
“Investigators are examining all available evidence and considering all potential motives, including whether bias played a role in the assault,” Hopkins Police Chief Brent Johnson said.
Police did not immediately identify the driver.
The Minnesota chapter of the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR) and the victim’s family identified him as Somali American Mohamed Yusuf.
“A passenger asked his name, told him he didn’t like that name and then he attacked him,” said Suleiman Adan, deputy executive director of CAIR Minnesota.
For Subscribers
The attacker tried to strangle the driver and then used the victim’s car to try running over him, according to Jaylani Hussein, executive director of CAIR Minnesota.
“This is one of the most heinous attacks that we have ever seen,”  Hussein said.

Uber said it was shocked by the attack. “We banned the rider from the Uber platform and are keeping the driver and his loved ones in our thoughts as we continue to support law enforcement with their investigation,” the company said in a statement.
Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison reposted a Somali news story identifying the victim with a picture of him in the hospital.
For Subscribers

“There will be accountability for this horrific crime,” Ellison added. “My heart breaks for Mohamed, his loved ones, and our Somali and Muslim communities apparently targeted by this assault. Everyone should feel safe and be safe in Minnesota — no exceptions. Hate and violence have no place here.”
Minnesota has become a hub for Somali immigration, and President Donald Trump has told Minnesotans to “fight back” against this community of recently arrived Americans.

The president has repeatedly verbally attacked Somalis, as well as Rep. Ilhan Omar, who was born in Somalia. Federal agents searched the lawmaker’s home last month in an inquiry of possible irregularities in her immigration process. Omar has denied any allegations and said she feels “confident in my truth.”

Trump’s attacks on Somali immigrants in Minnesota come in the wake of reports last year about dozens of people of Somali descent who were convicted of fraud schemes. Since then, Trump has called Somalis “crooks” and referred to Somalia as “filthy, dirty, disgusting, dirty.”
Somali immigrants are living in “fear, hatred, bigotry and demonization” that’s “come from the highest office of the land,” according to Hussein.
“This rhetoric has built an environment that we are living in today, an environment which we believe has created this heinous attack that took place on Saturday night here in Minnesota,” he added.
Hopkins Mayor Patrick Hanlon asked the public for time to allow department investigators to do their work.

“We ask for the community’s patience and understanding as investigators work diligently to determine the full circumstances surrounding this case,” the mayor said. “All of our investigators have been working non-stop to follow up on evidence and determine the facts.”

summary: Gifting doesn’t have to be hard. We rounded up 100 foolproof gifts that won’t end up in the regift pile, including gifts for techies, foodies, skin care obsessives and more.

Some people pride themselves on always knowing the perfect thing to give for the holidays, a birthday or any life milestone that’s typically celebrated with a thoughtful present. If you’re not one of those people, holiday shopping, or any shopping for that matter, can be extremely difficult.

That’s why we curated a list of the 100 best gifts we’ve ever given or received. Skin care, hair care and beauty
Theraface Pro

Though I love skin care, I wouldn’t usually spend more than $50 on a singular product. The Theraface Pro is an exception. It combines luxury skin care and technology, and though the 8-in-1 solution is pricey, it gives you so much: light therapy with red, blue, and purple LED light, microcurrent lymphatic therapy, three percussive attachments for massaging, and a cleansing ring. It comes with a stand and conductive gel, plus has an associated app that shows you how to use each treatment and provides you with routines to help address your specific skin concerns. - Jem Alabi, editorial operations associate
Rhode Peptide Lip Treatment

I’m not one to obsess over a celebrity-owned brand, but Rhode’s lip treatment really hooked me and now I have three tubes. It’s the ideal gift, in my opinion, especially if you’re using it as a stocking stuffer or white elephant gift. Lip balm is practical, first of all, but people might not want to buy Rhode’s formula themselves due to the $20 price tag. It comes in an unscented variety and four flavors — I’m addicted to the vanilla option. I find the formula moisturizes my lips really well, making them feel soft and adding lots of shine. - Zoe Malin, reporter
Shark FlexStyle

The Shark Flexstyle is by far one of the best gifts I’ve ever received. I have long, frizzy hair, and this tool cut my blow-drying and styling time from around 40 minutes to under 20 minutes. The five attachments also give it so much versatility, so I can decide to opt for a blowout look or bouncy curls depending on the day. - Caitlin Cusack, associate social media editor
Learn more: Shark SpeedStyle and SmoothStyle review: Hair care tools that (mostly) live up to the hype
We can help you find
Glossier You Rêve Eau de Parfum

Glossier’s entire You line is a win in my book, but this scent was the sleeper hit that unexpectedly became my daily fragrance. It has notes of buttercream, plum butter, iris and toasted almond, making for a warm scent that’s not too sweet or too floral. I love that it clings to the skin and lasts all day, and I get compliments from friends, co-workers, and strangers on the street every time that I wear it. - Ashley Morris, associate reporter
Jodsone Gel Manicure Set

I got my sister this manicure set for Christmas a few years ago, and she still uses it weekly. The kit comes with everything you need to give yourself the perfect at-home manicure, including 55 colors, as well as a nail lamp and other essential tools. You don’t have to be a nail artist to enjoy it — it’s super easy to use and make your nails look professional every time. She has saved so much money doing her own nails with this and has gotten endless use out of it. (I’ve even tried it a few times myself, too). - Georgea Hall, page
Learn more: The best nail strengtheners of 2025
Rare Beauty Soft Pinch Liquid Blush

Last year, my sister and I unknowingly got each other this blush for Christmas. With just a tiny dot’s worth of product, this gives the perfect amount of pigment and blends into my skin so smoothly. A little goes a long way, so one of these bottles can last what feels like a lifetime. - Cusack
NuFace Mini+ Starter Kit Microcurrent Device

I have a friend who will try any beauty tech device dedicated to warding off wrinkles and sagging, so when I received a NuFace microcurrent device for testing, I knew I’d have to buy her one. I use it as one of three products to keep my neck from sagging and my chin from doubling. She’s loves it for smoothing out the look of wrinkles. We’re both always told that we look at least 15 years younger than we are so it must be doing something — genetics are strong but they can’t get all the glory. - Shalwah Evans, senior editor
Dior Lip Glow Oil

A makeup artist friend who used to work at Sephora gave me this lip oil, and she said to me then what I’m saying now: It’s the best lip product I’ve ever used. It has a thick texture that glides onto my lips smoothly, and doesn’t feel sticky when I rub my lips together. I also love that it has a subtle color that I can build up or wear lightly, depending on the occasion. - Morris
Charlotte Tilbury Airbrush Matte Bronzer

This bronzer isn’t just my favorite bronzer — it’s my favorite makeup product. The only downside is that it’s expensive, and while it lasts awhile, as someone who wears bronzer every day, it still runs out sooner than I’d like. Because of that, it’s long been a favorite gift of mine to receive. It’s a natural shade that doesn’t leave me looking orange and blends seamlessly into my makeup and down my neck. It also layers well, so when I’m tanner in the summer I can still use the same shade. This one specifically is refillable, so extra refill pans can make a good stocking stuffer too. - Kailey Sigoda, NBC Selected intern
Eilish Eau de Parfum

This is one of my favorite perfumes, not just because of its best subtle vanilla scent, but the longevity on the skin was surprising. I was gifted this two years ago and the bottle seems never ending even after daily wear. The scent is a warm finishing layer that adds a nice sweetness to any fragrance combo you have, and the scent lasts all day.  - Imani Moten, NBC Page
Miss Dior Hydrating Body Milk

Miss Dior is the last layer that I put on before perfume. It melts into my skin without making it feel oily and greasy. The scent is light and floral and isn’t overpowering or hardly noticeable. With daily wear it lasts me about a year and pairs well with any summer or winter scent combo. - Moten
Tech
Apple iPad 11-inch

I actually didn’t think I’d had much use for an iPad, but after getting one for Christmas a few years back, I can indeed confirm that I was sorely mistaken. These days, I use this almost as much as I use my phone — it’s like my favorite cookbook, streaming device, and computer all in one. It’s small and easily portable, so I like to use it as a laptop replacement during longer days out. It’s also the perfect size for bringing along to activities like picnics, friend hangouts and more. Aside from streaming in bed, I especially like using it while traveling, since it’s the perfect size for fitting on my lap or on plane and train tables. - Morris
Learn more: What to know about the Apple iPad Air M3
Waterproof JBL Go 3 Speaker

This speaker has been with me since my freshman year of college. I didn’t actually know it was waterproof until I accidentally dropped it in my toilet and thought all hope was lost. It comes with a loop that makes it easy to carry/attach for transport, and is small but mighty. The sound quality is great, it works while charging, and connects instantly with my devices. - Alabi
Aura Digital HD Picture Frame

Something my loved ones and I have in common is that we all love taking photos and videos of special moments, but we never print them out to hang in our homes or put in albums. Aura’s Digital Frame is my solution to that, so now I gift it to people all the time. Your giftee downloads an app and uploads an unlimited amount of photos and videos to it. The app syncs with the frame, which displays all their content and automatically swipes through it during the day. Your giftee can add new content to the frame any time, and give loved ones access to it so they can share their memories, too. You can even preload your loved one’s frame with photos before they unwrap it, so when they plug it in for the first time, they see all their favorite people, places, pets and more. The frame also has a built-in speaker that can play audio from videos, and it automatically turns on and off depending on the lights in a room due to its built-in sensor. - Malin
Twelve South AirFly View Wireless Airplane Bluetooth Adapter

The frustrating part about earlier AirFly models was figuring out whether your headphones were actually connected, checking the remaining battery and switching from a device you used on your last trip. The new AirFly View addresses all of that by adding a built-in screen and I love it. - Josh Rios, video producer
Adjustable Cell Phone Stand

I initially sought out a phone stand because I like to use my phone for recipes, and I’m constantly on FaceTime. This one has been wonderful for lowering my screen time and relieving joint stiffness in my hands from typing all day. This stand is very sturdy; it comes assembled and has grips on the bottom so it doesn’t move. You can charge your phone through it, plus it’s wonderful for watching shows or reading on planes and buses. - Alabi
Beats Fit Pro (1st Gen)

I gave these to my brother as a Christmas gift one year, and he raves about the sound quality and comfort. They have some top-tier audio modes and have pretty decent battery life, too: You can get up to seven hours on a single charge and up to 30 with the case, according to Beats. - Cory Fernandez, commerce editor
Toniebox 2 Audio Player

My young niece and nephews are very fun to shop for. The Toniebox was a great addition to their screen-free home because it kept the kids entertained with stories and songs without tantrums. Even though my niece is reading now, she still enjoys popping her favorite character onto the Toniebox every once in a while. - Lauren Swanson, editorial director
Nintendo Switch 2 + Mario Kart World Bundle

The original Nintendo Switch was great — the Nintendo Switch 2 is better. It’s all the fun and portability of the original with more powerful components to play games with more detailed, immersive graphics. And new games like “Donkey Kong Bananza” and “Mario Kart World” are a ton of fun. The bundle linked above includes the console and code for Mario Kart World, so whoever you gift this to can start playing immediately. - Malin
Crosley Voyager Vintage Record Player

I love music, but I’m not passionate about having the most tricked-out tech, record players included. My mom gifted this to me because she knows that while I don’t need the fanciest model, I do appreciate aesthetically pleasing accessories. I think it’s the flower design (and affordable price) that makes this particular one giftable for record player newbies. Otherwise, it would just be boring. - Nikki Brown, senior SEO editor
Furbo 360° Dog Camera

When I first got my puppy seven years ago, I got the original Furbo as a gift to keep an eye on her while I’m away from home — and I’ve used it nearly every day since. Not only does it offer some peace of mind when I leave my dog alone, but it’s a great way to prevent her from doing anything she’s not supposed to (like ripping up toys or scratching furniture). I can talk to her via Furbo’s two-way audio, so she knows exactly when she’s doing something wrong. It also has a treat-tossing feature, so I can reward her for good behavior. Though I still have the stationary version of the pet camera, I gave my parents the higher-tech, 360-degree model when they adopted their new puppy last year. - Mili Godio, updates editor
Vankyo Leisure 470 Pro Projector

My mom bought me this projector for Christmas more than five years ago, and it’s still a staple in my bedroom. It can project a resolution of up to 1080P, and I love using it to watch my favorite movies and shows on my bedroom wall. It creates an immersive experience that allows me to really get lost in what I’m watching (I like to call it a homegrown dupe for the theatre experience). Since I can only use it when it’s dark, I also like that it keeps me from getting too distracted with TV during the day. - Morris
JVC Apple CarPlay Bluetooth Digital Media Receiver

My first car was a 2006 Jeep Liberty — not the most high-tech or modern car. I wasn’t able to connect my phone to Bluetooth, so I was stuck listening to the radio for my first few months of driving. My mom got me this digital media receiver for my birthday, and it changed my entire driving experience. I was finally able to listen to my own music, plus connect to Apple CarPlay, which allowed me to use voice text and calls, maps and more. - Cusack
Focusrite Scarlett Solo 3rd Gen USB Audio Interface

I got this from a friend who knew I was looking for an upgrade to my office audio setup. I often do voice-overs for our videos here at NBC Selected and need it to sound good. This sturdy red box always gives me peace of mind that I’ll get high-quality audio with every recording. It’s something I always recommend to people who are trying to step up their audio game. - Rios
Skylight Calendar 2

There was a time in my life when sparkly jewelery and fancy handbags got me excited. But now I’m a mom of two and nothing feels more luxurious than an organized life — and this calendar helps me get just that. You can sync your entire family’s individual calendars to it and color code entries to make it easier to read at a glance. You can even take photos of flyers or events and they’ll automatically upload to the calendar. On top of a calendar, you can make to-do lists for your kids or spouse and create a grocery list that anyone in the family can add to. At this point, the brand really should pay me to be an ambassador — that’s how many people I’ve recommended it to and bought it for. - Bethany Heitman-Samuda, commerce reporter
Photodom i217 35mm Point and Shoot Film Camera

I gave one of my best friends this camera as a dual birthday gift and travel accessory last year, and now, he takes it with him on all his vacations, outings and more. It gives photos the distinctive 35mm grain that we know and love, and it’s compact and easy to travel with. - Morris

The warming bulb in the lamp melts candle wax quickly, so you start to smell the scent almost immediately, and the light is dimmable, plus it has a built-in timer. The lamp’s height is adjustable, too, which is much more useful than I expected it to be. Even when I don’t turn it on, I love looking at the candle warmer, which I put in my apartment’s entrance so it’s front and center. I’ve also gotten tons of compliments on it — if any of my friends like it, I usually end up buying it for them, usually as a housewarming gift. - Malin
Easyplant Jade Pothos

When I moved into my first apartment, my mother-in-law gave me this Easyplant Jade Pothos as a housewarming gift. Since I don’t have the greenest thumb, this was the perfect gift: It has a self-watering pot, so I couldn’t over- or under-water it. Six years later, it’s still alive and thriving, despite me moving to a new apartment. Better yet, this particular indoor plant doesn’t need much sunlight to grow, which is great for my tiny, brick-facing apartment. - Godio
Qutool Shredded Memory Foam Pillows

I got this for my mom one Christmas because she, like me, is a hot sleeper. This pillow prevents your face and neck from overheating and is suitable for all sleep positions, according to the brand. It’s available in a body pillow and travel-friendly size, too. - Fernandez
Cast Iron Pigeon

My best friend is obsessed with pigeons and most gifts around the weird bird are often calendars or nothing that really shows your dedication. That’s why when I came around to this statue on my search for bird-related gear, I was so excited. It feels like a gift that can survive multiple moves and falls, while also showcasing her love of the fowl in a heavy crafted statue. - Rios
Badesofa Bath Pillow

There are two kinds of people in the world: people who love baths and people who hate them. I am the former, and this pillow is for people who are especially passionate about soaking at the end of a long day. This pillow is definitely too big for my very small bathroom but it also makes lying in the tub way more comfortable, so I accept the tradeoff. The material reminds me of outdoor patio furniture yet it doesn’t feel too firm or irritating on my skin. I haven’t timed exactly how long it takes to dry but it’s definitely not more than a couple of hours. - Brown
Artifact Uprising Pressed Glass Photo Ornament

I had my eye on this photo ornament last year, but I contemplated buying it for too long — before I knew it, I was taking my Christmas tree down, so it didn’t make sense to buy. This year, however, I’m way ahead of the game. I collect ornaments, and have one for each of my pets, so with a new puppy in the family, I had the perfect excuse to add this Artifact Uprising trinket back to my cart. I got one for each of my cats and one for my dog. They’re even more beautiful in-person. The brass frame and tempered glass make the ornament look like a cherished antique, and it’s double-sided, so I can see the pictures from all angles. Each ornament came with a ribbon I’ll tie in a bow around a tree’s branch. - Malin
Learn more: We tested popular photo book services — these are our favorite
Saje Aroma Om Ultrasonic Diffuser

I realized I was becoming a candle hoarder about five years ago and decided that I needed to approach home fragrance in a less wasteful way. I received this as a gift and it’s one of the most used products in my apartment since. The ceramic cover adds a classy vibe to my space and it barely makes noise when in use. The design is also versatile: I’ve redecorated many times and never had to consider removing this from any of my side tables. I started out with the brand’s essential oils but you can honestly pair it with any. Just be sure to clean the plastic water tank periodically (once a week if you’re using daily). Otherwise, it’ll get buildup. - Brown
RoLife Book Nook Kits

One of my favorites pieces of decor in my apartment is this small replica of a reading nook that I gifted myself after a stressful doctor’s appointment. It gave me a fun reason to put my phone down and focus on something tactile instead of doomscrolling and overthinking. This one took me a couple of days and with a battery (not included), it can double as a nightlight. - Brown
Birdfy Smart Bird Feeder

My dad is a gadget freak — he loves an electronic trinket, a fancy wind chime, basically anything that you’d find in an in-flight catalog. But, when you throw nature and data into the mix he’s like a kid in a candy store. The Birdfy was the perfect amalgamation of those things. He gets HD footage, instant alerts and even data about the birds patronizing his feeder. It isn’t just a gift — it’s a front‑row seat to feathered drama. - Swanson
Harlem Candle Company Josephine Luxury Candle

I received this candle as a gift a few years ago as a thank you from a friend and I keep repurchasing it. I know this sounds weird but it really does make my home smell like a chic speakeasy on 125th Street. I like that it’s not so expensive that someone would fall in love with the gift and then be deterred from replenishing it, bust cost a decent amount of money that someone receiving it would feel like you cared enough to spend a little coin on them. - Evans
Bouqs Magnolia Wreath

There’s not much that my 99-year-old grandma needs or wants for Christmas, except for spending time with family. So, every year, when I visit her in Chicago, I also send a magnolia wreath from Bouqs to hang over her fireplace. It makes her smile and helps holiday-ify her home for visitors. - Swanson
Quince European Linen Deluxe Bedding Bundle

I told a friend that I only had two sets of sheets, and they were appalled. They then got me a set of European linen sheets from Quince as a gift. Quince has a ton of colors to best match your room and vibe. And my favorite feature is the tag that states which way the top of the sheet is so you don’t have to guess and keep re-arranging them while making your bed. Now I own about four Quince sheet sets and feel like my friend’s gift really pushed me to upgrade my bedding. - Rios
Kitchen, cookware and appliances
Le Creuset Stoneware Mini Round Cocotte

I got one of these as a gift years ago and was first confused as to what I might make in it. It turns out it’s perfect for tons of things, like storing salt or serving yogurt or oatmeal. Since it’s oven safe, it’s also great for baking a single portion of a baked breakfast or for serving soup. It comes with a lid, too, which helps ensure even cooking. - Fernandez
Ember Temperature Control Smart Mug 2

I like my coffee hot — like, boiling, burning your throat hot. So, it’s a huge pet peeve of mine when my morning coffee starts to cool down after a few minutes. After watching me put my coffee mug in the microwave several dozen times a day, my family gave me the Ember Mug 2. Now, I can control and adjust the temperature of my drink using the associated app on my phone. The app lets me set the temperature of my coffee anywhere between 160 degrees and 185 degrees Fahrenheit, and while the hottest setting isn’t quite hot enough for my preferences, it prevents that dreaded sip of cold coffee. The brand has since launched the Ember Mug 3, which you don’t need the app to control. - Godio
Learn more: The best espresso machines for making barista-quality lattes at home
Papier Recipe Journal

My roommate is a serious baker and home cook, and for years I watched her constantly find and try recipes from the web without saving or filing them away. This recipe journal from Papier was my giftable solution — it has pages dedicated to keeping track of recipes and ingredients, so she can record and tweak her creations as she pleases. It’s also a great way for her to disconnect while cooking, so she can put away the screens, relax, and focus on the food. - Morris
Anthropologie Icon Juice Glass

As a fan of both Anthropologie’s glassware and themed decor, these juice glasses are some of my favorite items in my house. Several of my friends have gifted me the Halloween versions of these glasses in honor of my favorite holiday, and I intend to buy myself more for the upcoming holiday season. The handblown glass looks beautiful, plus each icon is unique and handmade. Keep in mind they’re very fragile and not suitable for hot beverages (I learned this the hard way). - Godio
Instant Pot Milk Frother

I gave this milk frother to my aunt one Christmas because she loves coffee and tea. It does all the work of heating up the milk and making it foam without burning the milk. It’s perfect for making hot chocolate too, in addition to the usual cappuccinos and lattes. You plug it into the wall and it has a plate to hold it in place. It’s also easy to pour without making a mess thanks to the spout. - Fernandez
KitchenAid Classic Series Stand Mixer

I’ve been baking for as long as I can remember, and was such a big baker as a kid that I asked for a KitchenAid stand mixer for Christmas at the ripe age of 8 years old. Obviously, it’s not the most conventional gift for an 8-year-old, but 15 years later, I still use that same KitchenAid stand mixer weekly, and it hasn’t failed me yet. I reach for it to make all kinds of things — cookies, bread dough, mashed potatoes and more. If the home cook in your life doesn’t already have a KitchenAid stand mixer, I’d highly recommend gifting them one — they might still be thanking you 15 years from now. - Cusack
Emile Henry French Ceramic Covered Bread Loaf

My husband bought this for my birthday this year after I put it on my wishlist and it has not disappointed me. First of all, it’s hefty. This thing is not going to just break from one little mishandling (which I may know from first-hand experience). It’s also beautiful, so when I cook my breads and loaves in it I feel lgood just serving right out of the dish. A bonus is that it comes with a top, so if you have food sitting out in it, you don’t have to worry about things just falling into the food. - Evans
Great Jones Dutch Oven

Great Jones’ Dutch oven was the first major “adult” gift I put on my wish list when I moved into my off-campus apartment in college. It’s a showstopper in any kitchen — its large oval shape, oversized handles and metal accent on the lid draw you in, and if you buy it in one of the brand’s vibrant colors (mine is in pastel pink), it can’t help but be the statement piece in your kitchen. I use it to make and serve big batches of soups, pastas and sauces, as well as braised vegetables and meats, so it helps me feed a crowd, which is my love language. It also retains heat very well and has allowed me to experiment with recipes, so it’s upgraded my cooking, too. - Malin
Keurig K-Mini Coffee Maker

I stole this Keurig in a white elephant gift exchange and did not feel bad about it at all. I have very little counter space in my NYC apartment, but this coffee maker fits perfectly into the corner of my kitchen. It makes a good cup of coffee, comes in super cute colors and won’t break the bank. I’ve gifted this to at least two friends so far, including to my brother when he moved into his college dorm. - Cusack
Drinkmate Omnifizz

I drink a lot of seltzer and other forms of carbonated water, so much so that I am sometimes inclined to make my own at home. I first tested the Drinkmate OmniFizz when I wrote our roundup on the best soda makers, and I love how easy it is to set up and use. I love using it to make my own flavors of soda and it helps me reduce how much “real” soda I drink, which is a great nutritional benefit. It doesn’t require any WiFi or smart features, all you have to do is install the cartridge and press the lever down to carbonate the water and then store the bottle in the fridge. - Fernandez
How we chose the best gifts ever

Our team of shopping experts created a list of the best gifts we’ve received over the years and gifts we’ve given that were met with great reception. Then we narrowed down our list to the top 100 products based on the following criteria:

Usefulness: While gifts don’t always need a practical use, we did consider whether these gifts actually make people’s lives easier. We included items that improve skin, could double as entertainment and a work tool, cooking gadgets and wellness products that assist with health tracking, among other things.

Value: Not every gift needs to last forever, in fact, edible gifts aren’t meant to last at all — at least not if they’re any good. Still, you want a gift that benefits the recipient. So, we considered the longevity and quality of products, thinking about the gifts we’ve given and received (plus the ones that overlap with our year-round testing) that have some serious staying power.

Giftability: To be clear: Anything can be a gift. Whether it wraps nicely into a box or bag has nothing to do with the giftability of an item. But we did consider the types of items that our loved ones may not purchase for themselves. Sometimes, that means something so practical that one doesn’t think to give (though the person receiving it is thankful to have it) or something so expensive that one holds off on buying it or wouldn’t buy for themselves at all.
Why trust NBC Selected?
Shalwah Evans is a senior editor for NBC Selected who oversees Selected 100 packages, including our ranking of the 100 best travel accessories and the 100 best Amazon products we’ve ever bought.

The NBC Selected editorial staff tests products regularly and has extensively covered many brands and product categories on this list. We frequently write about skin care, tech, travel, health and wellness and more. To curate this list, we relied on gifts our team has either given or received over the years and tried to include presents across different price points and categories.

title: The Hatch Baby is the one thing I tell every new mom to buy — here’s why
summary: I’ve used the Hatch Baby sound machine and night light with both my kids for nearly six years. Here’s why it’s the one product I tell new moms to buy.
story: When I became a mom, I didn’t just get a baby. I got a membership card. Nobody tells you this part, but becoming a parent automatically signs you up for a club. If you’re lucky, the other members show up right away. Mine did. Fellow moms swooped in to listen when I needed to vent, to share the hacks that got them through the newborn fog, and to tell me which products — strollers, car seats, baby bags — would actually make my life easier and which ones I could skip.

Now that I’m a mom of two, I’ve moved from new recruit to the welcoming committee. A few weeks after a friend tells me she’s pregnant, she always texts: “Okay, what do I actually need?” It’s a fair question. There’s an overwhelming amount of baby gear out there, and it’s hard to know what’s essential and what’s just clever marketing. I have a long answer about swaddles and bottles and which gadgets to pass on. But I always tell them to put one thing at the top of their registry: a Hatch Baby.

I don’t recommend much baby gear without a caveat. Most of what we bought lasted a few months before it ended up in the basement or the donation pile. The Hatch Baby is the exception. My daughter is nearly 6 and my son is nearly 2, and there’s one in each of their rooms — it has been part of our bedtime routine since the first week of each of their lives. Not only does it help them sleep better, it makes my life easier, too. And that is exactly why it is one of the products I talk about most often. Not familiar with this genius device? Read more about it below.
Hatch Baby

The Hatch Baby is a combination sound machine and night light that allows you to control the volume, sound and light right on the device. Then, the Hatch app helps with setup and advanced features like schedules, favorites and customization. The available sounds include white noise, ocean, rain, fan and thunderstorm, plus lullabies like “Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star.” The light settings are also customizable, so you can choose color and brightness. It also works as a sleep trainer for older babies and toddlers, using light cues to show them when it’s time for bed and when it’s okay to get up. For example, you can set it to stay red during sleep hours and turn green when it is okay for them to leave their room in the morning.

What sets the Hatch Baby apart from a basic sound machine is the sleep help that comes with it. Hatch gives parents the option to chat with certified sleep consultants and sleep guides. That support comes through Hatch+. Three months of Hatch+ are included in your purchase — after that it costs $5 a month or $50 for a year. While you don’t need a subscription for the sound machine and night light to work, Hatch+ is needed to access the full premium library and additional features, such as premium stories, songs, dynamic lights and sleep-support content. Every purchase also comes with free shipping and returns, a 30-night bedside trial, and a 1-year product warranty.
Who is the Hatch Baby for?

The Hatch Baby is for every expecting parent, and it’s what I’d put at the top of any baby registry. It’s especially helpful if you have a noisy home, whether that’s caused by a barking dog, a busy street or an older sibling who’s still awake. Down the road, it’s a lifesaver for toddlers and preschoolers who wake up before the sun. It makes a great baby shower gift, because the recipient will use it for years.
What I love about the Hatch Baby

We have a French bulldog who barks a lot. At delivery trucks, at the doorbell, at nothing at all. I was adamant that nap time would not feel like a game of chance. The Hatch’s white noise has been our best defense. It creates a steady wall of sound that muffles the barking, so my kids stay asleep instead of popping up every time the dog decides he needs to yell at the wind blowing.

The best gear changes jobs as your kid grows, and this one does exactly that. When my kids were babies, the Hatch Baby was a dim light for middle-of-the-night feeds and a sound machine to help them settle. In the toddler years, it became a sleep trainer. When transitioning my daughter out of her crib and into a regular bed, I create a new schedule on her Hatch.

Thirty minutes before bed, the sound machine turns down at a quiet level. This is her signal that it is time to start winding down. Then, at bedtime, the light turns red and stays that way until she is allowed to get out of the bed the next morning. When it is okay for her to get out of bed, the light turns green. Having these signals has helped her understand what is expected of her and when, and she loves the routine of it.
Any parent knows that the creak of a bedroom door can undo an hour of rocking. Being able to turn up the volume, dim the light or switch it off from my phone is game changing.

This is the feature I talk about most. Little kids can’t read a clock, but they understand colors. I set a schedule in the app so my daughter’s light glows one color when it’s time to sleep and changes to another when she’s allowed to leave her room in the morning.

It turned our mornings from a negotiation into a routine. She knows the rule, the light keeps track of it and I’m no longer the bad guy. Because the schedule runs every day on its own, I set it once and only adjust it now and then when her bedtime changes.
A few things to know about the Hatch Baby
If you haven’t picked up on it by now, I will say it plainly: I love the Hatch Baby. But, as with any product, there are a few things you should note before you decide to get one for yourself.

It needs an outlet. The Hatch Baby has no battery, so it has to stay plugged in. That also means it won’t keep running during a power outage.The app is necessary. Power, volume, sound and light can be controlled on the device itself. But schedules and customization happen in the Hatch app. I also find the app to be an easier way to switch the sound and light, even though those things can technically be done on the device.Hatch+ is optional. Three months of Hatch+ come with the device. After that, you don’t need to pay anything for the sound machine, light and bedtime and wake-up cues to keep working. A subscription, however, gets you access to extras like premium stories, songs and sleep-support content.
